💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Volkswagen ID Buzz has not been a big hit in the US (where it’s just too expensive and doesn’t even provide a lot of range), but it’s still one of my favorite vehicles.
  • In a recent development, however, the manufacturer has just rolled out a latest version of the ID Buzz that is designed to allow for easy sleeping within the van.
  • Interestingly, you can get this camper version of the van in either the 5-seat or 7-seat version of the ID Buzz.

The Volkswagen ID Buzz has not been a big hit in the US (where it’s just too expensive and doesn’t even provide a lot of range), but it’s still one of my favorite vehicles. I would certainly have one in my driveway if I had enough money for one. Part of what makes the ID Buzz so appealing is how it reminds one of the VW Hippie Bus of yesteryear, but that vehicle was super low cost as well as versatile and useful. The ID Buzz is sort of a deceiving imitation of that model, as it’s quite expensive (especially in the US) and doesn’t really provide a lot of extra utility compared to what’s on the market today.

In a recent development, however, the manufacturer has just rolled out a latest version of the ID Buzz that is designed to allow for easy sleeping within the van. The “camper” version of the ID Buzz has a few special features for this. Also, just to reiterate, it’s not cheap. So it’s more a little luxury camper van for people with money than a way to get around and live freely for young people scraping by and vagabonds. The ID Buzz Beach, as it’s called, will start at around £54,000 in the UK. (Whether it will come to the US and at what price, who knows?) It includes the following:.

Interestingly, you can get this camper version of the van in either the 5-seat or 7-seat version of the ID Buzz.

According to recent reports, is this going to attract a lot of buyers? Almost definitely no. Is it super cool, though? I think so.

#122306. Put To The Test, Those Special Engine Cleaning Oils Do Some Lifting

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (532 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

Put To The Test, Those Special Engine Cleaning Oils Do Some Lifting

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (532 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Motor oil naturally helps to flush out common contaminants, and there's a whole supply of products specifically made to keep the mechanical parts of a vehicle clean and running.
  • It has been revealed that the Motor Oil Geek is Lake Speed Jr., of SPEEDiagnostix, known for its used oil analysis services.
  • Using those skills, he put three "cleaning" motor oils up to the test: Mobil 1 Advanced Clean, Valvoline Restore & Protect, and Pennzoil Ultra Platinum.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Motor oil naturally helps to flush out common contaminants, and there's a whole supply of products specifically made to keep the mechanical parts of a vehicle clean and running. From Top Tier gasoline complete with detergents to some types of engine motor oil — these treatments and additives are designed and marketed to you, the consumer, to keep things clean internally so your car lasts. Do they really do what they claim to do, though? The Motor Oil Geek on YouTube put those "cleaning" oils to the test to see if they do make a difference.

It has been revealed that the Motor Oil Geek is Lake Speed Jr., of SPEEDiagnostix, known for its used oil analysis services. Speed himself is a Certified Lubrication Specialist and OIl Analyst who used that expertise to help Joe Gibbs Racing for 12 years — a testing ground sometimes more brutal than the testing cars go through in-house.

Using those skills, he put three "cleaning" motor oils up to the test: Mobil 1 Advanced Clean, Valvoline Restore & Protect, and Pennzoil Ultra Platinum. There's actually a fourth oil, Valvoline Premium Blue Restore Gen2 — but that's a separate, yet important test, also included in the video. The results didn't match what real in-engine testing produced, but even in this comparable bench testing scenario, these oils managed to clean up expectations.

The Motor Oil Geek put the three oils through what's called an ASTM sequence IIIH test, which is a standard test used to evaluate engine oils at high temperatures and high speeds. Typically, these tests are conducted in an actual running engine for 90 total hours, broken down into four 20-hour test segments and one 10-hour segment. For bench test purposes, Speed ran the oils for 168 hours with varying temperatures from room temperature to 150 degrees Celsius, to better emulate real-time conditions of an engine from cold runs to high-speed performance.

He used pistons with considerable deposits from a turbocharged Mini Cooper engine, each marked with a letter code to track which one was tested in what oil. Those pistons were sent off to be professionally rated before the test, as well as after, to measure improved "cleanliness.".

Industry observers note that three of those pistons were then hung separately from a device so they could soak in an oil in 1000 mL beakers over a magnetic stirring hot plate. It's a way to control the important aspects of the test concerning time, temperature, and agitation (movement), so Speed could focus on the concentration and cleaning. The fourth piston was soaked in the Valvoline Premium Blue Restore Gen2, which claimed it could clean parts just soaked in the oil.

It has been revealed that in the end, all four oils cleaned some of the deposits on the pistons. The most improved was the fourth piston that soaked in the oil, which The Motor Oil Geek explained contains an agent called Ester, also used in two-stroke oils to keep things clean. And keep in mind, they perform even better in a running engine. So, if you're at all worried about buildup slowing you down, these cleaning oils might actually do the trick.

Why Warming Up Your Car Unattended Is Illegal In Some States And Cities

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (673 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as a seasoned driver, you may be aware that some states' roads are more dangerous in winter.
  • Industry observers note that the reason behind the laws is rather simple: Those puffs of smoke in the chilly air indicate a running, usually unlocked, vehicle.
  • It has been revealed that all is not lost for the dedicated puffer, though, as there is an exception to the rule.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as a seasoned driver, you may be aware that some states' roads are more dangerous in winter. Did you also know that four out of five of these states, as well as 27 others, have laws against puffing? No, not that puffing. Puffing, or "car puffing," is a slang term for the ritual of letting your car get warm and toasty before driving off. This is usually accomplished by starting your car and then heading back inside for a bit. The term comes from the telltale puffs of smoke that can be seen coming out of the tail pipe.

Industry observers note that the reason behind the laws is rather simple: Those puffs of smoke in the chilly air indicate a running, usually unlocked, vehicle. This makes it an easy target for crime. Someone can jump in and take off in your vehicle in a matter of seconds — not good for anyone involved.

It has been revealed that all is not lost for the dedicated puffer, though, as there is an exception to the rule. Vehicles equipped with a remote starter are often exempt from these rules, as a remote start system allows you to keep your vehicle locked and your keys in your pocket.

We get it — getting into a cold car sucks. But having your car stolen sucks even more. Even beyond your own personal grief, stolen vehicles are often used in subsequent crimes. Also, items left in your vehicle, such as registration information, can be used for identity theft, and a garage door opener can become easy access into your home. According to the National Insurance Crime Bureau, "By the end of 2021, just over 100,000 thefts facilitated by keys or key fobs were reported nationally. This total accounts for 11% of vehicle thefts of all types reported in the U.S. in 2021.".

It has been revealed that outside of the crime aspect, there are other reasons to avoid puffing and other forms of idling. Cold weather already hurts your gas mileage, and burning gas while you're not moving is only going to make that worse, costing you money in the long term. On the environmental side, according to the U.S. Department of Energy, "It is estimated that idling personal vehicles generate around 30 million tons of carbon dioxide (CO2) every year," which is roughly the equivalent of adding an additional 5 million vehicles to the roads.

Back in the olden times — sometime after the last horse and buggy but before the first DeLorean — it was common knowledge that you had to let your car warm up before driving it. So, a little puff session before work was thought to be good. That is an outdated notion today, and, in fact, experts such as AAA declare that a modern vehicle only needs a few seconds to warm up. Excessive idle time can stress the engine, as it isn't running at its preferred temperature.

Laws against puffing are clear that leaving a running car unattended is a no-no. One pro tip based on this definition is to warm up your car while you are shoveling snow out of the driveway, scraping ice off of the windows, or performing any of the other tasks that make up the unbreakable laws of winter driving. That way, you have an eye on the vehicle and are taking care of your pre-driving chores.

Puffing-specific laws are on the books in the following states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Kansas, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, and Wisconsin. If you live in one of these states, check your local statutes to see how the law may affect you. One final note to all the EV owners out there: It is recommended that you warm up your vehicles while they're still plugged in, preventing you from burning too much energy.

#122295. Latest Update: Mazda Miata Engine Swaps Ranked Best To Worst (For Your Budget And Your Patience)

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1520 w)
📖 Baca

Latest Update: Mazda Miata Engine Swaps Ranked Best To Worst (For Your Budget And Your Patience)

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1520 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jalopnik has long maintained that the Mazda Miata is the answer to every question.
  • According to recent reports, but Miata enthusiasts are a crafty bunch, and over the nameplate's 37-year history, their quest for more power has driven the development of camshafts, turbochargers, and, of course, engine swaps.
  • Sources indicate that not all swaps are created equal, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jalopnik has long maintained that the Mazda Miata is the answer to every question. What's the best affordable convertible? Miata. What if you want a fun commuter that's reliable and sips fuel? You should consider a Miata. What if you want a car to take off-road? Surprisingly, the Miata is the answer again. Emme Hall won her class in a Baja race with her off-road modified Miata. It's an excellent sports car, relatively cheap, abundant, and just plain fun. Over four generations, the only only real critique of the venerable roadster is that it's never been particularly quick in a straight line.

According to recent reports, but Miata enthusiasts are a crafty bunch, and over the nameplate's 37-year history, their quest for more power has driven the development of camshafts, turbochargers, and, of course, engine swaps. Swaps are not for the faint of heart – they often consume a lot of time and capital — but they are a great way to add power without the complexities of a forced induction setup on the factory engine.

Sources indicate that not all swaps are created equal, though. For example, transplanting an engine from a newer Miata will be easier and cheaper than shoehorning a V8 into the engine bay. However, the V8 will net you way more power for the extra effort and money. There are so many Miata swaps out there — from Honda K24 four-cylinders to Toyota V12s — so we have compiled a helpful a list of engines that go in Miatas, organized from the cheapest and easiest to the most difficult and expensive.

The easiest Miata swaps involve upgrading to a larger Mazda motor within the same engine family. Early first-generation Miatas (1990 to 1993) were equipped with a 1.6-liter four-cylinder. Its output was a tepid 116 horsepower. Luckily, later first-generation cars (1994 to 1997) and all second-generation cars (1999 to 2005) came with a more powerful 1.8-liter four-cylinder that will bolt up to the factory transmission. Flyin' Miata sells an affordable kit that makes the swap to the 1994-to-1997 engine essentially plug-and-play. The later engines make more power, but they still require some effort to work in the 1.6 cars. To get the most power for your money and effort, look for a 2001-to-2005 Miata engine donor. They have variable valve timing and provide 142 horsepower .

Sources indicate that similarly, third-generation Miatas (2006 to 2015) have an easy path to more displacement and power. A 2.5-liter Duratec four-cylinder engine from a Ford Fusion, Mazda3, Mazda6, or Mercury Milan fits in place of the Miata's 2.0-liter four-cylinder with minimal effort. The larger engine is plentiful in junkyards and can be had for as cheap as $350. The swap isn't completely plug-and-play — the Miata's lower intake manifold needs to be modified to fit the 2.5 — but most of the 2.0-liter's accessories fit the larger engine without issue. A stock 2.5 makes about 10 more horsepower and 35 more pound-feet of torque over the factory Miata engine. But with upgraded cams and a freer-flowing exhaust, Grassroots Motorsports made 196 hp at the wheels with its 2.5 swap.

In a recent development, under the hood, the Miata has never had much more than an economy-car four-cylinder turned sideways. By contrast, when Honda decided to make a roadster of its own, the automaker equipped it with the F20C four-cylinder — an engine with a 9,000-rpm redline that held the title for the most naturally aspirated horsepower per liter until the Ferrari 458 came along. Intrepid engine swappers may think a Miata with an F20C could be a good way to create a low-buck, bootleg S2000. But S2000 engines aren't exactly affordable or easy to come by.

However, there is another Honda option that can rev almost as high as the F20C and makes similar power. Enter the K24, the budget friendly and readily available alternative. The K24, like its name might suggest, is a 2.4-liter four-cylinder with dual-overhead camshafts and Honda's i-VTEC system. The high performance variants of the engine found in the Acura TSX and Honda Civic Si make around 200 horsepower in factory trim. But the aftermarket for the engine is immense, and with the right combination of parts, the K24 has the potential to make nearly 300 hp without boost.

Although it was only available in front- and all-wheel-drive cars, tuners like KPower Industries recognized the engine's potential for rear-wheel-drive applications. As such, KPower Industries makes kits to swap a K24 into all four generations of Miatas. It's not a simple or cheap swap. Bits like a transmission adapter plate and a standalone ECU are needed to make it all work, and the most comprehensive kits start at around $6,000. But for a powerful, lightweight engine that doesn't mess with the balance of the Miata chassis, the juice is worth the squeeze.

The next rung on the Miata-swap ladder is the V6. A V6 swap is an exercise in more — more cylinders, more power, more effort, and more money. There are three V6 engines that have readily available Miata swap kits: the 3.5-liter Honda J35 found in the Odyssey and various Acuras, the direct-injected 3.6-liter GM LFX found in the Chevy Camaro and Cadillac CTS, and the 3.0-liter Jaguar AJ30 V6 found in the S-type and XJ. Each option has an aluminum block and heads, and depending on the variant, outputs roughly 40 to 100 more horsepower than a stock K24.

No matter what engine you choose, the kits are not cheap. Luckily, with a kit, you don't have to fabricate your own front subframe, motor mounts, and other swap-related parts. The Honda J35 kit from Mini Tec is the most affordable at $3,350, and it utilizes the factory Miata transmission and differential. But that doesn't include any provisions for the cooling, power steering, and fueling systems. The next kit on the list is the $7,260 GM LFX V6 conversion from V8Roadsters, which requires a Camaro transmission and other GM donor parts. This adds more complexity to the swap, but the GM parts are more durable than the factory Miata stuff. Rocketeer Cars takes the most comprehensive approach to V6 swaps. It will sell you everything you need for the conversion, including a refreshed Jaguar AJ30 V6. But that will set you back roughly $22,040. If you are going to spend all of that money on a V6, you might as well go for the gusto and consider our next swap option.

Sources indicate that if the Miata is the universal answer to any sports car question, the Chevy LS is the the answer for any engine swap inquiry. The V8 LS-series engines are still such a popular swap for a reason. They're compact, powerful, readily available in junkyards, and have massive aftermarket support. The LS engine is available in many configurations, from 4.8-liter truck engines to 7.0-liter sports car screamers. Even the wimpiest 4.8-liter LS can make 400 horsepower without much effort. That type of power is a tantalizing prospect for those looking to make a modern version of a Shelby Cobra with a Miata. Fortunately, for those with enough capital and bravery, the substantial V8 can be stuffed into every generation of Miata. Although Colorado-based tuner Flyin' Miata stopped doing V8 swaps years ago, other manufactures like Monster Miata and V8Roadsters will sell you the parts to roll your own.

It has been revealed that there are many tradeoffs involved in putting an LS in a Miata, first of which is the car's balance. Monster Miata says the weight distribution moves from a perfect 50/50 to a nose-heavy 53/47 with a major V8 under the hood. Also, the rest of the Miata's driveline can't hold up to V8 power, so it needs to be swapped as well. You'll need parts like a T-56 six-speed transmission, fresh driveshaft, and a differential from a fith-gen Camaro. Costs are highly variable depending on which engine you choose, but they generally fall somewhere around $20,000 for the average completed swap.

Industry observers note that A Miata with more than eight cylinders is like an automotive cryptid. There's evidence that it exists, but it can only be found in the murky depths of internet forums and YouTube. During our dive into the internet swamps, we found a Miata with a Viper V10, one with a Jaguar V12, and another with a Toyota 1GZFE V12 from a Toyota Century.

The efficacy of these swaps is questionable, as there are no off-the-shelf kits for them. And more cylinders means more weight over the nose of the Miata, even further messing up the roadster's weight distribution compared to an LS. Plus, an LS can make just as much power or more power than the engines above. The LS also fits in the engine bay a whole lot better. The guy who did the Jaguar V12 swap noted he had to cut the firewall and move it 6 inches back. But if you're crazy enough to try one of these swaps, you'll certainly have the only Miata at the Cars and Coffee with more than eight cylinders.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that OLMEDO, Spain, Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that the milestone follows AGCO’s September 2025 announcement of its 10-year VPPA with BRUC.
  • According to recent reports, “Project Olmedo will give AGCO long-term price certainty for the majority of the electricity certificate cost in Europe,” mentioned Tim Millwood, Senior Vice President, Chief Supply Chain Officer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that OLMEDO, Spain, Nov. 19, 2026 — AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) today announced that Project Olmedo, the solar installation at the center of its first Virtual Power Purchase Agreement (VPPA), has completed construction and commissioning and is expected to begin delivering renewable electricity to the Spanish power grid in the coming months, pending final regulatory approvals. BRUC, one of the largest renewable energy groups in Spain, built the new solar installation in the northwest province of Valladolid.

Recent findings suggest that the milestone follows AGCO’s September 2025 announcement of its 10-year VPPA with BRUC. The installation’s two solar projects, Los Silos and El Granero, span approximately 300 hectares (741 acres) and hold approximately 150,000 solar panels. AGCO’s portion of the installation’s annual production is expected to be approximately 150 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of renewable electricity a year, equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of approximately 40,000 European households, based on Eurostat data.

According to recent reports, “Project Olmedo will give AGCO long-term price certainty for the majority of the electricity certificate cost in Europe,” mentioned Tim Millwood, Senior Vice President, Chief Supply Chain Officer. “In volatile energy markets, securing that stability for 10 years strengthens the resilience of our supply chain while supporting fresh renewable generation.”.

According to recent reports, A VPPA lets a organization support new renewable energy projects without taking direct delivery of the electricity they generate. Because AGCO’s agreement supported the construction of a brand-new installation, it will add new renewable capacity to the grid rather than drawing on existing sources, a principle known as additionality. The agreement also helps reduce AGCO’s Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased electricity in its Europe/Middle East (EME) region and supports its commitment to reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 55% by 2033 from a 2022 baseline.

“Additionality is what makes this agreement truly meaningful,” said Roger Batkin, Senior Vice President, Corporate Affairs, General Counsel & Corporate Secretary. “We did not simply buy renewable electricity that already existed; we supported the construction of a brand-fresh renewable solar project. Accomplishing this project required over two years of involvement from many teams, functions, and areas of expertise across AGCO, along with technical advisory support from Schneider Electric and a strong partnership with BRUC.”.

Reflecting AGCO’s Farmer-First strategy, Project Olmedo supports local farmers to further diversify their land use by leasing land for the project while maintaining the option for livestock to graze among the panels, maintaining the vegetation in place of machinery.

Recent findings suggest that AGCO and BRUC leaders, joined by local community representatives José Emilio Escudero García, Mayor of Bocigas, and Ursino Vara Pérez, Mayor of Almenara de Adaja, marked the milestone with a ribbon-cutting ceremony at the site in November. Additional drone footage from Project Olmedo and the ribbon-cutting event are available on AGCO’s YouTube page.

For more details on AGCO’s sustainability initiatives, visit the company’s sustainability webpage and read the 2025 Sustainability Report. For more information about BRUC, visit the company’s website at brucenergy.com.

AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) is a global leader in agricultural machinery and precision agriculture technologies. Driven by a Farmer-First strategy, AGCO delivers value through its differentiated leading brands, Fendt™, Massey Ferguson™, PTx™ and Valtra™. AGCO’s high-performance equipment and smart farming solutions, including brand-agnostic retrofit technologies and autonomous offerings, empower farmers to drive productivity while sustainably feeding the world. For more information, visit www.agcocorp.com.

According to recent reports, coinbase is bringing crypto trading directly into ChatGPT as competition for AI-powered financial services intensifies. Meanwhile, PancakeSwap has dropped “Swap” from its name, expanding beyond decentralized trading. The two developments show how Coinbase and Binance-linked crypto projects are positioning themselves for the next phase of digital finance.

Coinbase confirmed its ChatGPT integration yesterday, allowing users to connect accounts and manage portfolios. Users can check balances, analyze holdings, and place eligible trades using everyday language. And every order requires explicit approval before execution.

The timing coincides with Pancake’s attempt to reposition itself beyond its original decentralized exchange business.

Trade Base assets from ChatGPT@ChatGPT now connects to your Coinbase account, so you can trade Base assets in chat pic.twitter.com/tg9r2Iv3Qe.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

Recent findings suggest that the Coinbase plugin allows eligible customers to trade crypto and equities without leaving ChatGPT. Users can request market or limit orders through conversational instructions.

Before execution, ChatGPT displays an interactive confirmation card showing order details. Customers must approve the transaction before Coinbase processes it through its Advanced Trade platform. Standard trading fees, eligibility requirements, and account limits still apply.

In a recent development, coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong described the integration as another step toward an emerging agentic economy. The idea involves AI assistants handling increasingly complex financial tasks for owners. But Coinbase still keeps humans responsible for approving individual trades for now.

To decentralize AI and preserve freedom, we need a coordination layer: a market economy where agents communicate and cooperate through prices.Teams of specialized open-weight models can outperform frontier models, just as a team of skilled people can outperform any single….

The integration also builds on Coinbase’s AI infrastructure. Its Coinbase for Agents toolkit provides developers with connections to trading accounts and market data. The ChatGPT launch brings those capabilities into a more accessible consumer interface.

Sources indicate that as of today, the official integration at the moment remains limited to eligible U.S. Coinbase users. It also depends on ChatGPT account and workspace availability.

newly introduced brand, who dis?PancakeSwap is now Pancake 🥞6 years ago we were known for one thing. Today, we’re More Than a Swap. Let us reintroduce ourselves 👇 pic.twitter.com/J3P7Mocu2P.

While Coinbase expands through ChatGPT, Pancake is changing how customers perceive its decentralized trading ecosystem. Formerly known as PancakeSwap, the platform announced its rebrand today. The upcoming identity reflects six years of expansion beyond its original token-swapping business.

Pancake now operates across more than 11 blockchain networks. The platform reports over 208 million users and more than $4.4 trillion in cumulative trading volume.

Sources indicate that its services now include perpetual contracts, tokenized stocks, ETFs, yield products, and developer infrastructure. The project is also preparing a dedicated mobile application. Its CAKE ticker and contract address remain unchanged, with existing staking positions unaffected.

According to recent reports, pancake’s relationship with Binance makes this rebrand interesting. Binance Labs unveiled a strategic investment in CAKE in June 2022. The investment supported the decentralized exchange’s development within the BNB Chain ecosystem.

Sources indicate that the rivalry becomes clearer when looking beyond the latest announcements. Binance has already introduced its own AI infrastructure through Binance Agent OS. Debuted in August 2026, the platform connects compatible AI applications with Binance trading, market data, wallet, and payment capabilities.

According to recent reports, its Model Context Protocol server supports compatible AI agents, including ChatGPT. Developers can build applications that access supported Binance services through user-controlled permissions.

Pancake is also developing its position in this emerging market. In July, the platform partnered with BNB Chain’s Agent Studio to help developers deploy autonomous agents.

Sources indicate that these agents can interact with Pancake’s liquidity pools, rebalance positions, and execute trading strategies. Its AI tools also include portfolio planning and assistance across DeFi products.

This creates an interesting contrast between the two ecosystems. Coinbase is bringing AI-powered trading directly to consumers through ChatGPT. Binance is building infrastructure that allows developers and AI agents to interact with its services. Pancake adds a decentralized execution layer to the wider BNB Chain ecosystem.

Sources indicate that the next battle in crypto may not be about which exchange attracts the most human traders. It could be about which infrastructure becomes the preferred destination for AI-powered financial activity.

#122288. Every Car Brand That's Put Rotary Engines In Production Cars (There Aren't Many)

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1157 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

Every Car Brand That's Put Rotary Engines In Production Cars (There Aren't Many)

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1157 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that beyond the realms of car enthusiasm, most normies wouldn't have actually heard of a rotary engine – also known as a Wankel engine (after Felix Wankel, the man who patented the design in the first place).
  • It has been revealed that when it comes to street cars, the most coveted example is Mazda's famous RX-7.
  • But Mazda isn't the only car brand to have ever used a rotary engine in its production cars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that beyond the realms of car enthusiasm, most normies wouldn't have actually heard of a rotary engine – also known as a Wankel engine (after Felix Wankel, the man who patented the design in the first place). These are fondly called "spinning Doritos" because at their heart is a triangular rotor that whizzes around a central shaft and makes power in a similar way to how a regular piston engine does. There are many pros and cons to rotary engines, and the cons are why they have seldom been used in automobiles.

It has been revealed that when it comes to street cars, the most coveted example is Mazda's famous RX-7. The same brand was also responsible for arguably the most mythical race car ever created: the quad-rotor 787B. It won the 1991 edition of the famed 24 Hours of Le Mans and leaves a lasting impression on anyone who hears it, thanks to the orgasmic, high-pitched wail it generates as it climbs toward 9,000 rpm.

But Mazda isn't the only car brand to have ever used a rotary engine in its production cars. The very first instance came from a German company called NSU (which eventually became part of Audi), and there were also examples from Citroën and the Russian brand Lada. Maxton, a low-volume sports car maker from the U.S., also briefly used rotary engines in the Rollerskate. But since it used Mazda engines and was built in such small numbers, it is often discounted.

According to recent reports, in fact, the famed Japanese brand is estimated to have built around two million rotaries between 1967 and 2012, starting with the much-loved Cosmo sports car and ending with the equally adored RX-8 coupe. It has since resurrected the rotary, but only as a generator that forms part of a hybrid package in the MX-30 electric SUV, so it hardly counts.

In a recent development, mazda really did try it all at the height of its rotary days, even building the now highly collectible Rotary Pickup. It was — and is — humanity's sole rotary-powered pickup truck, equipped with a 110-horsepower 1.3-liter Wankel unit, and made purely for the U.S. and Canadian markets. The firm built around 15,000 examples, and well-maintained, low-mileage trucks still go for close to $30,000. Further afield, ardent enthusiasts will also remember the Mazda Furai concept, which is among the weirdest one-off cars ever built.

In a recent development, before Mazda's love affair with Wankels, NSU rolled out the very first rotary-powered production car, the Spider, at the 1963 Frankfurt Auto Show. Its single-rotor, 500cc engine wasn't hugely powerful: it produced just 50 hp when it debuted, and maxed out at 54 hp in its most powerful guise. Despite getting positive reviews from the automotive press, the Spider never really took off. Just 2,400 units are estimated to have been built before production ended in 1967.

Recent findings suggest that NSU replaced it with the Ro 80, which was a sleek, four-door sedan with a 115-hp twin-rotor motor and a fancy independent suspension. It was so good that European Car of the Year jurors voted it as their winning candidate for 1968 – making it the first German vehicle to ever win the coveted prize. It enjoyed a 10-year run rolling off the production lines, with NSU building around 37,000 examples before retiring it in 1977.

In a recent development, it was in 1964 that Citroën struck up a partnership with NSU to develop rotary engines. While NSU went on to join the VW Group, Citroën stayed the course and eventually unveiled the M35 in the late '60s — its first true rotary-powered car, built in a limited run of 267 examples. Based on an Ami 8 – the same model James May used during the "Top Gear" classic time trial rally challenge in Mallorca – the M35 even had Citroën's super-soft hydropneumatic suspension, with 49 rampant French horses under the hood.

Recent findings suggest that then came the GS Birotor in 1973, whose twin-rotor setup produced an even mightier 106 hp and allowed for a top speed of 109 mph. Citroën eventually dropped its rotary experiment by the late '70s, in part due to low sales volumes, but also because of the world's oil crisis. The latter is significant here because rotary engines, by nature, guzzle fuel. They burn a lot of oil, too.

Recent findings suggest that yes, who'd have thought it? Little about these cars ever made it past the Iron Curtain, but Lada started its Wankel journey in 1978 with the VAZ-21018. Though it may have shared model codes with a fax machine of some kind, the 21018 did have a pretty prominent place in society. The four-door sedan used a 71-hp rotary engine that was basically reverse-engineered from either an NSU or a Mazda engine, depending on who you ask, and proved horribly unreliable. Some accounts say these engines couldn't manage more than 12,000 miles before succumbing to problems such as seal and bearing failures.

Lada took another crack at it in 1982 and created a twin-rotor engine with two outputs: 115 and 140 hp. These were fitted to the VAZ-21019 sedan, and provided a notable step up in performance from "regular" Ladas. They proved slightly more reliable too, at the cost of poorer fuel economy. Lada did stick by its rotary engines all the way until the early 2000s, albeit on an increasingly small scale, before wrapping up production entirely.

Citroën, Mazda, Lada, and NSU aren't the only manufacturers to have dabbled with rotary cars. General Motors was at the height of its power in the '70s, and saw an opportunity to reinvent how vehicles were engineered by placing rotaries at the heart of its prepares. It had intended to offer its then-fresh Vega compact car with a Wankel engine, and committed $50 million just to license the technology. There was even the Aerovette: the best-looking Corvette of all time that never made it out of the concept stage and had a rotary engine. Unfortunately, as would soon happen with Citroën and the GS Birotor, the global oil crisis forced GM to ditch its rotary plans by the end of 1974.

Recent findings suggest that mercedes-Benz also got in on the act with its jaw-dropping C 111 experimental vehicle, first previewed at the 1969 Frankfurt Auto Show. It seemingly had everything a discerning celebrity would've wanted back then: a funky wedge-shaped body, a striking orange metallic paint job, and gullwing doors. Whereas the very first experiment had a three-rotor configuration, the second cranked it up to four rotors and was claimed to have a top speed of 186 mph. It all sounds super exciting, right? Well, Mercedes chose not to put it into production. Sorry to burst your several-second dream of owning one. But of the rotary-powered cars that did make production, which would you most like to own?

#122284. Charles Lindbergh Flew 3,610 Miles Despite The Disadvantage Of Not Having A Windshield

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (886 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

Charles Lindbergh Flew 3,610 Miles Despite The Disadvantage Of Not Having A Windshield

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • First off, let's keep in mind that Charles Lindbergh wasn't the first person to fly across the Atlantic Ocean.
  • In a recent development, naturally, that achievement took a special kind of plane, so LIndbergh's Spirit of St.
  • Of course, the engineers had to find a place to put all that fuel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

First off, let's keep in mind that Charles Lindbergh wasn't the first person to fly across the Atlantic Ocean. Some 66 to 80 people had already made the trip before him. Lindbergh, though, became the first person to fly solo and nonstop, from Upcoming York to Paris, in 1927.

In a recent development, naturally, that achievement took a special kind of plane, so LIndbergh's Spirit of St. Louis had been modified for the attempt. And perhaps most importantly, that meant making room for enough fuel to cover his route of more than 3,600 miles. In the end, the plane carried 450 gallons of the stuff, an amount that weighed 2,750 pounds, representing more than half the craft's gross vehicle weight. Yep, that GVWR is as important for pilots as for RV and truck owners.

Of course, the engineers had to find a place to put all that fuel. The result was that the Spirit of St. Louis featured a main gas tank in front of Lindbergh's seat and extra tanks in the wings. Now, carrying all that fuel made sense, given the flight's nonstop nature. But Lindbergh had requested that the forward tank should fit between the engine and the cockpit for safety reasons in case of a crash. That may seem counter-intuitive, but Lindbergh was apparently worried about being crushed between the engine and fuel tank if the latter was mounted behind the cabin.

Industry observers note that you can probably see where this is going, but Lindbergh certainly couldn't. With a large gas tank directly ahead of him, he had no way to look out the front of the plane. So it wasn't like the Spirit of St. Louis lost its windshield in flight, exposing Lindbergh to the elements. It didn't have a windshield in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that lindbergh had a few tricks up his sleeve when it came time to fly the Spirit of St. Louis, starting with one he picked up in his days as an airmail pilot. Packed into relatively small planes crowded with bags of mail, he developed the skill of looking out his side windows to fly the craft. In fact, modern pilots are still taught how to use the so-called "Lindbergh Reference" method when something blocks their forward vision. It's basically a way of learning to use just the view from the left-hand corner of a windshield to understand a plane's roll, pitch, and yaw.

Helping matters — at least somewhat — was a retractable periscope Lindbergh could extend from the left-side window. The scope wasn't exactly easy to use, however. Lindbergh had to rely on a small mirror mounted to the instrument panel to get a view. Still, it's too bad that modern cars with terrible visibility don't have something similar.

Industry observers note that some modern pilots may wonder what the major deal is about Lindbergh not seeing what was in front of him, since flying, taking off, and landing can all be accomplished today in zero visibility. Well, the Spirit of St. Louis lacked the kind of sophisticated technology that makes that sort of feat possible. Heck, Lindbergh's plane didn't even have a radio or gas gauges — he kept track of fuel by penciling marks directly on the instrument panel. It all seems to have worked out, though. After taking off from Newly introduced York's Roosevelt field on the morning of May 27, 1927, he touched down at the Le Bourget Aerodrome in Paris 33½ hours later.

It has been revealed that logically enough, Lindbergh was sharply focused on the airplane's range — which explains why he carried so much fuel and so little else. Not only did he ditch the radio, he said goodbye to the parachute, navigation lights, and even a traditional pilot's seat. He sat on a wicker chair instead, designed his own lightweight flying boots , and skipped unnecessary maps.

The work paid off, as the unladen Spirit of St. Louis weighed only 2,150 pounds. Built for Lindbergh's transatlantic flight, it was based on a Ryan M-2 mail plane and adapted to meet the challenge. For example, its wings were stretched to a span of 46 feet, which required a longer tail, too. Meanwhile, the forward-mounted fuel tank extended the fuselage. The outcome was an overall length of more than 27 feet.

In a recent development, providing motivation for the aircraft was a Wright J-5C Whirlwind engine. The air-cooled nine-cylinder mill delivered 220 horses and was known for its durability. Experts at the time claimed the motor could run for 9,000 hours, giving Lindbergh a cushion of roughly 8,965 hours in the Spirit of St. Louis. FYI: The plane was named for the city that hosted the first real gas station in the nation; it in St. Louis that Lindbergh found a group of businessmen to sponsor the flight.

It has been revealed that also, in an odd bit of foreshadowing, Lindbergh had a "Native American swastika" painted in the plane's nosecone for good luck. Just nine years later, he discovered a different use for that symbol at the 1936 Olympics in Berlin, where he and his wife were special guests of Nazi leader Hermann Goering. Lindbergh must have liked what he saw, as he became a full-on Nazi sympathizer and antisemite.

#122282. Industry News: The EV Takeover Is Taking Shape, Despite Heroic Efforts To Stop It

📖 Baca

Industry News: The EV Takeover Is Taking Shape, Despite Heroic Efforts To Stop It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1110 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whelp, the AI boom has had one positive knock-on effect.
  • Sources indicate that I’m just going to stick my neck out and say that the eponymous Aptera solar-powered autocycle from the US startup Aptera will attract enough AI-enriched drivers to make a go of it.
  • Industry observers note that autocycles were once common here in the US and overseas markets, distinguished from motorcycles by their front-facing seats and steering wheels, rather than straddled seats and handlebars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whelp, the AI boom has had one positive knock-on effect. It is creating fresh multi-millionaires by the bushel, any one of whom can afford to splurge on a pricey new electric vehicle. That aside, EV stakeholders in the US are springing back to life after a year-long slumber. Even General Motors is in play, stirring up long lost memories of its 1990’s-era EV1 debacle instead of hiding its head in shame. What’s up with that?

Sources indicate that I’m just going to stick my neck out and say that the eponymous Aptera solar-powered autocycle from the US startup Aptera will attract enough AI-enriched drivers to make a go of it. The on-again, off-again, on-again automaker has been on this year, working towards volume production of a plug-in, three-wheeled two-seater EV that can travel up to 40 miles on its own solar-plus-storage system (see more Aptera news here).

Industry observers note that autocycles were once common here in the US and overseas markets, distinguished from motorcycles by their front-facing seats and steering wheels, rather than straddled seats and handlebars. They fell out of favor in the US by the middle of the 20th century, but 21st century hot-rodders have revived the form with a focus on eyebrow-raising, open-air, gas-guzzling showpieces. In particular, interest has spread in states that do not require autocycle drivers to invest in an additional motorcycle license.

According to recent reports, the Aptera is showy in its own right, resembling a rocket ship with unique aerodynamic styling. Perhaps it may even show up in the next James Bond adventure with James Pattinson at the wheel. In the meantime, the tech giant has just made good on its pledge to reward early investors in the world’s first solar-powered car with the first production models to role off the assembly line. Aptera #1 goes to the founder and CEO of GDP Venture, Martin Hartono, aka “Accelerator #1.”.

Drivers can reserve an Aptera of their own for just $100, and they can expect to pay about $40,000 for the ride. Considering that the solar fuel is free, anyone in the mood for a head-turning ride will get quite a bargain for their $40,000 compared to other competitors in the zero emission two-seater field, such as the recently refreshed Tesla Roadster.

Speaking of refresh, General Motors has been weirdly lavishing attention on the EV1 sedan all this year, even though the automaker has been roundly criticized for the killing the short-lived car in its cradle. The automaker began producing EV1 electric sedans starting in 1996, following the unveiling of its Impact electric concept car in 1990. Unlike the Impact, EV1 was designed for use on the road. However, it was also designed mainly for the California market, and primarily for lease, not for sale. Production halted in 2003 at just about 1,000 vehicles, all to be recalled by GM and sent to the crusher as chronicled in Chris Paine’s 2006 documentary, “Who Killed The Electric Car?”.

Or, maybe not so weird after all. GM’s electrification journey long predates the launch of Tesla Motors in 2003. The legacy automaker is now determined to stake out its claim on automotive history, with 2026 marking the 30th anniversary of the start of EV1 production.

GM has been celebrating the anniversary all this year with multiple long form articles about the Impact and EV1 on its website, eager to remind everybody that its industry-leading vehicle electrification efforts of the 1990’s continue to manifest decades later, in the form of heat pumps for climate control, by-wire technology, and regenerative braking among other elements.

Sources indicate that GM’s latest love letter to the EV1 popped up on November 17, when the automaker officially celebrated the completed restoration of the EV1 “V212” alongside its a private owner, Billy Caruso. The rare survivor of GM’s the junkyard crusher was evidently hiding out in an impound lot in Georgia all these years, until Caruso acquired it at auction and enlisted Jared Pink of the popular show The Questionable Garage to fix it up. Considering TQG’s large following on YouTube, GM wisely lent its engineers to the effort, along with several donated parts from its own EV1.

US President Donald Trump and the Republican majority in Congress have made a heroic effort to dial down the vehicle electrification movement, but facts on the ground keep getting in their way. For starters, today’s advanced batteries apply across multiple energy resources, fossil and non-fossil alike. So, it’s no surprise to see the US Department of Energy continuing to throw taxpayer dollars at new energy storage projects (here’s one example), even though some of that activity will eventually ripple into the vehicle electrification field.

Industry observers note that the US Department of Defense is also getting into the act. DoD’s electrification journey has been a tedious one, but in recent years it has begun creeping stealthily towards a vision of ground mobility enabled by electricity, providing the key tactical advantages of silent running and a low heat signature.

The latest news on that score involves a $1.4 billion loan commitment from DoD’s Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), enabling the silicon-based battery materials startup Sila to vault its signature product into commercial production. DoD’s primary interest in the company consists of applications in the electric drone and autonomous mobility fields, but Sila has long been eyeballing the EV market as well.

According to recent reports, sila secured the loan commitment in August, and it has not let the grass grow under its feet. On November 18 the company declared an off-take agreement with the well-known Tesla EV battery supplier Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America. “The multi-year agreement is part of a long-term commercial relationship with the potential for over $1 billion of offtake over time,” Sila explained in a press statement, further elaborating that Panasonic will deploy its proprietary Titan Silicon silicon-carbon anode material in battery cells.

It has been revealed that “The partnership is also expected to support significant manufacturing and construction job creation in the United States. With Sila’s U.S.-based anode production underpinned by proprietary American technology and know-how, Panasonic and its OEM customers gain a clearer path toward a more secure, resilient, and sustainable domestic supply chain,” Sila emphasized.

In a recent development, that’s…interesting! Aside from Tesla as one of Sila’s OEM customers, keep an eye on another Panasonic offtaker, the up-and-comer US startup Harbinger Motors, which also has a foot in the DoD door.

Photo: The vehicle electrification movement is far from over in the US, with the startup Aptera among the stakeholders betting on an EV sales rebound in the coming years (cropped, courtesy of Aptera).

Is AI A Public Or A Private Asset?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1126 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that isabelle Ferreras is a professor and research director at the University of Louvain, an Accelerator fellow at the Institute for Ethics in AI at the University of Oxford, and a senior research associate at the Center for Labor and a Just Economy at Harvard University.
  • Sources indicate that she told The Guardian this week that she has grave concerns about the way AI and the corporations promoting it are managing this brave newly introduced technology.
  • Sources indicate that last month, a person responsible for overseeing safety reports at OpenAI left the tech giant, claiming its culture was “broken.” He added that the entire AI industry was careless when it comes to developing AI technology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that isabelle Ferreras is a professor and research director at the University of Louvain, an Accelerator fellow at the Institute for Ethics in AI at the University of Oxford, and a senior research associate at the Center for Labor and a Just Economy at Harvard University. It safe to say she knows a thing or two about computer technology and AI.

Sources indicate that she told The Guardian this week that she has grave concerns about the way AI and the corporations promoting it are managing this brave newly introduced technology. Her concerns are spurred by the number of high profile computer engineers who have quit recently over fears that AI development is out of control.

Sources indicate that last month, a person responsible for overseeing safety reports at OpenAI left the tech giant, claiming its culture was “broken.” He added that the entire AI industry was careless when it comes to developing AI technology. The month before that, a researcher at Anthropic — which went public yesterday at a valuation $1.8 trillion dollars — warned that AI “could kill us all by the end of the decade.”.

“When the only way for a conscientious engineer to raise the alarm is to leave,” Ferreras remarked. “it is a clear sign that corporate governance in the industry is broken. Each departure takes with it the very knowledge needed to steer these systems safely. We cannot regulate AI safely from the outside if the companies building it remain autocracies on the inside.”.

In a recent development, ferreras warned that governments think of AI either as a “consumer product to be tested for defects or as a geopolitical race to be won by relaxing rules on business. Corporate lobbyists encourage this view as a trade-off between safety and innovation by arguing that legislation imposes too many burdens.

Sources indicate that “This is a dangerous path. AI is not merely a software product. It is a technology of government. Yet inside frontier labs such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, and Google, a handful of executives and capital investors decide which values are coded into models that shape millions of lives,” she stated.

According to recent reports, interestingly, Michael Connolly, the award winning author of the Bosch and Lincoln Lawyer novels, published a book last year in which the family of a young woman, who was murdered by her boyfriend after he interacted with an AI agent, sues the organization behind the AI agent. The essence of the lawsuit is that AI only does what it is programmed to do, and since the lead programmer of this particular AI agent was a misogynist in real life, it reflected his values when it interacted with humans. The book is called The Proving Ground and it is a fascinating read.

Recent findings suggest that while Ferreras applauds those who warn of the malignancies built into AI, she pointed out that humans have short attention spans. “Time and again, a safety researcher or engineer walks out of the door with a public warning that commercial pressures are overriding safety guardrails. As a society, we applaud the courage of these individuals and debate their warnings for a news cycle — and then we move on. But we miss the deeper institutional failure those resignations reveal. As the great political scientist Albert Hirschman made clear, exit is not voice.”.

In a democratic society, the exercise of governing power requires the consent of the governed, Ferreras told The Guardian. “Yet corporate law still treats firms as the property of shareholders, and the labor investors, who put their intellect, health and lives into the firm, as subordinates. To align AI with the public interest, we need a dual strategy: alongside solid public regulations on AI ‘from the outside,’ we need to enter the corporate black box and force corporate governance into alignment with democratic principles.”.

An analogy can be made to the Federal Communications Commission, which licenses broadcasters and promotes the free flow of information to the public. The digital world thinks such controls are archaic, but the lack of them is a clear and present danger to a civil society.

Ferreras suggested that “governments must outlaw non-disclosure and non-disparagement clauses that silence staff on safety risks, and enact robust whistle blower protection. Tech workers also need a collective standing over corporate strategy, independent channels to report safety breaches, and formal representation inside frontier labs before models are deployed.”.

It has been revealed that in addition, she argued that “legislators must establish a binding right to co-decision over workplace AI. No algorithmic system that monitors, evaluates or disciplines workers should be deployed without prior negotiation. At national and EU level, we need to consider collective bargaining on AI deployment and veto rights for works councils or trade unions, backed by independent technical experts and a strict ban on automated firing.”.

In a recent development, lastly, she supported the democratization of boardrooms and rewarding firms that refuse to concentrate power at the top. “Legislators should mandate worker-elected directors on boards, moving towards dual-majority governance in which strategic decisions require the consent not only of capital but of labor.” Some, like Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg, would characterize her suggestions as liberal claptrap, and they would be correct. Ferreras would happily unravel the “tech bro” manosphere in order to promote a more open and just society.

It has been revealed that she pointed to the research by Daron Acemoglu and Simon Johnson, the 2024 Nobel laureates in economics, which demonstrates that technological revolutions do not automatically produce shared prosperity. Instead, institutions decide who benefits and who pays.

Industry observers note that “Extending democracy into the firm is not an old battle over power for its own sake, but a practical necessity for more ethical judgment. Aligning AI with the good of workers and society requires more wisdom than closed executive rooms can offer. It needs what the Yale political theorist Hélène Landemore calls ‘democratic reason’ — the collective intelligence of diverse, deliberating voices, brought to bear on corporate decision-making,” Ferreras wrote.

It has been revealed that “Left to self-regulation and the occasional whistleblower, AI governance will entrench an unaccountable algorithmic oligarchy. Accountability and alignment begins with giving those who build these systems and those whose work they govern an enforceable voice, from the code floor to the boardroom.”.

Ferreras’ point of view is decidedly liberal, and yet her arguments are clear and concise. How can we give so much power to digital agents and not take reasonable steps to ensure the needs of society as a whole are respected? The tech industry enjoys almost unfettered freedom of action today. It may be time to consider whether that is a good long term strategy.

US to install 36% more wind turbines in 2025 than previous year

📅 18 Dec 2025 | ⏱️ 4 min read (751 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Windpowerengineering

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the United States is expected to add more than 7 GW of wind installations in 2025, a 36% increase over the previous year, and the five-year outlook remains unchanged quarter-over-quarter from previous forecast, according to the “U.S.
  • Sources indicate that amid a challenging market environment, the report shows that the United States is on track to add 46 GW of new wind capacity from 2025 to 2029, with total projected volumes unchanged quarter-on-quarter from previous forecasts.
  • According to recent reports, while Q3 installations came in 23% below forecast at 932 MW, the market has shown progress with 3.8 GW queued for Q4 2025 — representing 52% of the year’s total expected capacity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the United States is expected to add more than 7 GW of wind installations in 2025, a 36% increase over the previous year, and the five-year outlook remains unchanged quarter-over-quarter from previous forecast, according to the “U.S. Wind Energy Monitor” report released by Wood Mackenzie and the American Clean Power Association (ACP).

Sources indicate that amid a challenging market environment, the report shows that the United States is on track to add 46 GW of new wind capacity from 2025 to 2029, with total projected volumes unchanged quarter-on-quarter from previous forecasts. However, timing has shifted, as 2026 and 2027 will deliver significant gains, at 10.7 GW and 12.7 GW, respectively, as more assets advance through the development pipeline.

According to recent reports, while Q3 installations came in 23% below forecast at 932 MW, the market has shown progress with 3.8 GW queued for Q4 2025 — representing 52% of the year’s total expected capacity. This back-loaded installation pattern is consistent with typical project-commissioning timelines.

U.S. turbine order intake has rebounded to pre-One Massive Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) levels quarter-over-quarter, supported by 2+ GW of firm commitments in Q3, the biggest intake in the region in the last nine months and a 79% quarter-over-quarter increase. However, true visibility remains limited as OEMs increasingly withhold project details and much qualifying “start-of-construction” activity occurs through off-site component manufacturing.

The market will then see a noticeable drop off, as 2029 weakens meaningfully quarter-over-quarter following project cancellations and inactive designations for late-decade capacity, driven by permitting and broader development challenges.

“The U.S. power market is facing mounting strain after a decade of flat demand, with utilities committing to 160 GW of large-load additions. This represents a significant opportunity for wind energy, which benefits from strengthened economic fundamentals and a compelling business case driven by its competitively low LCOE,” remarked Leila Garcia da Fonseca, director of research at Wood Mackenzie. “However, turbine costs remain elevated due to tariffs and mid-term wind growth will depend on resolving permitting and policy uncertainty.”.

Recent findings suggest that power demand growth through 2029 is expected to average around 3% compared to just 0.7% over the previous decade, with data centers accounting for approximately 59 GW of the 90 GW total peak demand growth. This surge in baseload demand positions wind as a natural fit to meet rising power needs.

The five-year capacity outlook remains unchanged at 39.8 GW of added capacity quarter-over-quarter. The 2025-2027 pipeline is fully committed with all projects having turbine orders in place. More than 60% of the three-year capacity outlook has been commissioned or is under construction.

It has been revealed that activity is led by western states, such as Wyoming, Fresh Mexico and others, that will account for 34% of activity in this time period. Major projects driving the outlook include Pattern’s 3.5-GW SunZia project in New Mexico, which will position the developer as 2026’s top installer, and Invenergy’s 998-MW Towner Energy Center in Colorado, the largest single project expected in 2027.

The market continues expanding geographically, with Arkansas bringing its first utility-scale onshore wind project online through Cordelio’s Crossover Wind.

The repowering market remains strong, as Wood Mackenzie projects that 18 projects will drive 2.5 GW of capacity additions in the next three years.

Industry observers note that wood Mackenzie expects the offshore installation pace to slow in Q4 2025 due to harsh winter weather conditions, pushing remaining capacity into 2026. Despite these near-term adjustments, Vineyard Wind has demonstrated strong execution, connecting 15 turbines in Q3 and delivering 200 GWh through nine months.

“U.S. offshore wind highlights diverging momentum,” stated Garcia Da Fonseca. “Projects under construction with COD estimated for 2026 continue to hit key milestones, but post-2027 developments face potential delays amid constrained wind turbine installation vessel capacity, driving delays and contract terminations.”.

The offshore sector is also experiencing significant financial pressure.

The report highlights that uncertainty around tariffs is a threat to projections. Wood Mackenzie projects that tariffs will drive up turbine costs in 2026, before moderating in subsequent years. In total, U.S. onshore wind capex is projected to increase by 5% through 2029.

Recent findings suggest that “U.S. wind turbine pricing is experiencing unprecedented uncertainty as conflicting market and regulatory forces interact,” remarked Garcia Da Fonseca. “Domestic manufacturing overcapacity relative to permitted project volumes, particularly after 2028, would normally place downward pressure on prices. Despite this, onshore wind costs are expected to continue rising due to tariff exposure on raw material inputs and subcomponents.”.

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

7 Long Distance-Focused EV SUVs Ranked From Best To Worst Range

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2415 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that both average latest-car prices and fuel prices are hitting record highs left and right.
  • However, despite some highly competitive offerings, EVs haven't quite popped off yet.
  • In a recent development, concerns about the range of EVs may have once been well-founded, but that's not so much the case anymore.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that both average latest-car prices and fuel prices are hitting record highs left and right. The state of things would be enough to get any car enthusiast down, if it weren't for the fact that electric cars are rad as hell. Fast, stylish, and fuel-efficient, EVs seem to get better with each new model that is released and each new generation that refines an already good vehicle into something great (we're looking at you, Toyota bZ).

However, despite some highly competitive offerings, EVs haven't quite popped off yet. The Trump administration's brutal murder of the EV tax credit and subsequent loosening of CAFE standards didn't help. The technology is still relatively fresh, so EVs are generally more expensive upfront than gas-powered cars, and there's also the question of range, one of the major specters haunting EV adoption at larger scales.

In a recent development, concerns about the range of EVs may have once been well-founded, but that's not so much the case anymore. Tons of electric vehicles, SUVs included, can now breach 300 miles on a charge, and several are pushing past the 400-mile boundary, too. With ranges like that, road tripping is more than feasible, say nothing of the 34 miles the average American drives per day.

Sources indicate that to illustrate the point, we've gathered a list of seven electric SUVs with excellent ranges — all over 300 miles on a full charge. This isn't a comprehensive list, but rather a sampling of the field, from awe-inspiring Lucids to affordable-ish Fords. To make the list, the cars needed an official fuel economy estimate published by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Perhaps unsurprisingly, more range is typically more expensive, and the longest-range SUVs out there are luxury vehicles, but a few more accessible rides made the list, too.

In a recent development, debuting for the 2027 model year, the BMW iX5 is a shakeup to the luxury EV SUV world in a couple of significant ways. For starters, this is the German automaker's first electric iteration of the popular (but once-controversial) X5. Iterating on a beloved idea is always sure to ruffle some feathers, but actually driving the iX5 might just unruffle those feathers right back down. The iX5 is also one of the exceedingly few EV SUVs that come close to matching the range of the Lucid Gravity. However, the iX5 actually dethrones the Gravity and takes the top spot among long-distance-focused EV SUVs. The icing on the iX5 cake is that it somehow manages to be even cheaper than its Lucid rival.

There's only one version of the BMW iX5 for its inaugural year, known as the iX5 60 xDrive, and it MSRPs at $81,250 with the destination fee included. This leaves the iX5 around $20,000 cheaper than the Lucid Gravity with the longest range. That's an impressive accomplishment, even if the iX5 doesn't quite stack up in other ways. To get the full 456 miles of range, you'll need to opt for BMW's 21-inch M Aero Polygon 1116 M wheels or the 21-inch Aero Double-Spoke Bicolor 1113 wheels with summer tires that can be chosen for no additional cost. Other available wheels result in a range from 418 miles to 447 miles. Still not bad.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to performance and style, the iX5 feels distinctly X5-like, though it reportedly doesn't handle quite as well. BMW advertises a 0-60 mph time of 4.4 seconds, which is slower than some rivals, and the iX5 also has less cargo space than the Gravity. Features abound, and the interior is comfortable and stylish.

Lucid Motors flipped the American EV world on its head when it debuted the Lucid Air, which had a maximum range of up to 517 miles. Then the mad lads did it again with the Lucid Gravity, which held the record for the longest-range SUV until the BMW iX5 came onto the scene. Still, the Gravity is a lot more than just an exceptionally long-range SUV that, admittedly, looks like a cooler minivan.

In our test, we found that the Gravity is just hands-down exceptional. The SUV has also earned astounding 10/10 ratings from both Car and Driver and U.S. News & World Report, and it consistently lands among the top two or three entries in its class in other major publications. It's lauded for its alacrity off the line, generous cargo area, and its refined interior.

According to recent reports, to get the most range possible, you'll need to get your hands on the mid-tier Grand Touring trim and keep the standard wheels, which are 20 inches in the front and 21 inches in the back. Other wheel options are available but reduce your overall range. This setup will run you $98,900 plus the $1,600 destination fee, which puts the Lucid Gravity GT just within the six-figure range before tax. In return, you get a screaming-fast 3.4-second 0-60 mph time, 828 horsepower, and the ability to charge up to 200 miles in under 11 minutes. And you get to drive one of the coolest cars on the road today.

Standard features on the Gravity GT include PerLuxe leather upholstery, 12-way power-adjustable front seats, a power liftgate, a 34-inch cockpit display, a 12.6-inch landscape pilot display, a wireless charging pad, a 10-speaker stereo, and tons of safety and driver assistance features. All-wheel drive is standard, but the optional third row reduces the range to 437 miles.

Industry observers note that the final 400-mile top dog on this list is the illustrious Rivian R1S. While Rivian has just recently dropped the smaller and better-than-we-ever-hoped-for 2027 R2 and has some of us biting our nails in anticipation of the smaller-yet R3, enthusiasts would be remiss to forget that the R1S is still a wildly impressive machine with monstrous off-road capabilities and up to a delicious 410 miles of maximum range. And on top of that, the R1S was one of just two large SUVs to earn the IIHS Top Safety Pick+ designation in 2026.

Another aspect that sets the R1S apart from its long-range competition is its status as a default seven-seater. While the Lucid Gravity offers an optional third row, the R1S is designed for it natively, and it's all the better for it. All three rows have adult-friendly legroom, even if getting all the way back takes some squeezing. The 2027 R1S starts at $85,885 for the base Premium trim with destination, and unlocking the full range requires upgrading to the long-range battery, which costs an extra $7,000. The setup produces 533 horsepower and can hustle from 0-60 mph in 4.5 seconds.

Industry observers note that the interior is spacious and comfortable, offering abundant head- and legroom in the first two rows and well-cushioned seats. The design aesthetic is modern and distinctly premium, featuring metal and wood accents and soft plastics. It's the electro-minimalism we're used to by now but done superbly. The R1S can tow up to 7,700 pounds when properly equipped and also has off-road chops for days, thanks to its high torque rating, good ground clearance and standard surround-view camera system. Like many EVs, it's screen-forward, almost obnoxiously so, but that's a small price to pay for greatness.

Say what you will about Tesla — from dodging hundreds of millions of dollars in taxes probably being a bad thing to the company's vehicles' being inextricably linked to Elon Musk's questionable politics — but the fallen automaker did help pave the way for some of the truly exceptional EVs we have today, and the Tesla Model Y was no small part of that. You can yet see some of that luster in the Model Y's still-impressive range of up to 355 miles — 3 miles more than the larger Model X's 352-mile maximum.

According to recent reports, the Model Y's range is a steep drop from the other luxury EV SUVs on this list, but it's important to remember that the above entries are the crème de la crème – the boundary-pushing pinnacle of EV design and the culmination of years and billions of dollars of R&D. They are, simply put, outliers among electric SUVs. Meanwhile, 355 miles of range is still far more than the majority of the field. And while the Model Y loses 55 miles of range compared to the R1S and its ilk, this Tesla is drastically less expensive up front. For the full 355-mile range, you'll need the standard-wheelbase Model Y Premium with rear-wheel drive, which runs a mere $47,630 with destination.

The downside, of course, is that you own a Tesla in a reality where the CEO appeared to have publicly thrown up a Sieg Heil. While the Model Y was once the world's best-selling car, it's been surpassed by many rivals in recent years. It has been knocked for its cumbersome touch controls, a stiff ride, and lots of cheap-feeling plastics. Sure, even the Long-Range Model Y Premium can sprint from 0-60 mph in 5.4 seconds (4.3 seconds with AWD), and has a spacious interior, but that's not particularly special anymore.

Hyundai has been killing it in the electrification game recently, and the Ioniq 9's introduction for the 2026 model year took the company's cred even higher. Made stateside, the Ioniq 9 is the most expensive Hyundai ever, with a starting price of $60,655 after destination fees. And while that's pretty pricey, you sure do get what you pay for. There's tons of space for both passengers and cargo, and the interior design is sleek and modern. It's also a three-row ride with room for six or seven, depending on the configuration, and the third row is largely adult-friendly. I'm a serial third-row hater, and I adored my time spent in the way back on the Ioniq 9. It's even easy to access, which earns it substantial points in my book.

It has been revealed that the lineup's best range of 335 miles is found on the base S trim, which uses a single-motor rear-wheel-drive setup that produces 215 hp and 258 lb-ft of torque. That's a lot less power than what you'll find above, meaning the Ioniq 9 is one of the slowest SUVs on this list, but a decent torque rating means it won't feel sluggish from a stop. Somewhat surprisingly, upgrading to a dual-motor trim with all-wheel drive only reduces the range by 15 miles while bumping the power output up to 303 hp, and it costs just $3,810 extra, which might just be worth it depending on how badly you need the extra range.

Standard features on the base S trim include cloth upholstery, heated seats, an eight-way power-adjustable driver's seat, a 12.3-inch touch screen, a wireless charging pad, and a whole seven USB-C ports. Factor in the Ioniq 9's long list of ADAS features, like Hyundai's Highway Driving Assist 2, pedestrian and cyclist detection, and traffic-sign recognition, and the price starts to feel justified.

Recent findings suggest that while you might balk at seeing the beloved Mustang name slapped on an electric SUV of all things (an SUV Mustang? Make it make sense!), this Ford actually is the real deal. When we talk about well-rounded cars, this is what we mean. Heck, the 2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E even has a soft-roader trim. The Mustang Mach-E is screaming fast, super charismatic, fun to drive, spacious, relatively affordable, and long-ranged. Finding something to dislike about this SUV involves a level of nitpicking that isn't worth getting into here. If you haven't found yourself inside a Mustang Mach-E, reserve all judgment until you do, and get in one as soon as possible.

To get the most out of the Mustang Mach-E's range, you'll need to get the rear-wheel-drive Premium model with the extended battery pack, which unlocks the full 320-mile range. The Premium trim starts at $41,090 and carries a $2,045 destination fee, while the battery upgrade costs an extra $4,750. This version of the Mustang Mach-E sports 272 hp and 387 lb-ft of torque, which is more than enough to make this crossover feel truly fun.

Industry observers note that the interior is upholstered with synthetic leather, and it's known to be comfortable and spacious in both rows, though you may want to stick to a maximum capacity of four due to the center column eating some of the rear middle legroom. The cabin design is centered around the Ford's 15.5-inch touch screen, which is vertically mounted and controls many car functions in addition to infotainment. Other standard features on the Premium trim include dual-zone automatic climate control, power-adjustable front seats with heating and ventilation, and ambient interior lighting. Despite the Mustang Mach-E not having seen a refresh in a few years, it still feels stylish and modern.

Coming in just shy of the Mustang Mach-E's 320-mile range is the 2027 Chevrolet Equinox EV at a very respectable 319 miles. The Chevy Equinox EV is what you might call the people's car. It's the least expensive SUV on this list by a few thousand bucks and a somewhat modest offering compared to the rest of the entries here, but it's by no measure a poor choice for EV shoppers.

The base LT 1 trim starts at $37,195 with destination. It's one of very few EVs under $40,000 that gets over 300 miles on a single charge, and you can get that mileage on any trim with front-wheel drive. Models with all-wheel drive lose about 12 miles of range, leaving them still solidly above the crucial 300-mile mark.

Recent findings suggest that the best way to describe the Equinox EV is perhaps to call it familiar and predictable. There's not much flashy about it, and it's not particularly sprightly with its 220 horsepower. Testers report the Equinox EV rides smoothly with engaging handling, but notably heavy understeer takes some joy out of taking the SUV through corners. However, as a practical car used for commuting, city driving, and the occasional road trip, there's not much to actively dislike. The interior is spacious, albeit not exactly beautiful, and even tall passengers will have space in the back row. The Equinox EV also dodged Chevy's recent EV recall involving faulty brakes, which is a major point in its favor.

In a recent development, on the base LT 1 trim, you'll get features like cloth upholstery, manually adjustable front seats, a couple USB ports, and a 17.7-inch touch screen. Safety features include forward collision alert, rear park assist, and Teen Driver mode.
