📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that 270 kW (367 PS), top speed of 240 km/h and 4.7 seconds from 0 to 100 km/h: With the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, Volkswagen is marking the 50th anniversary of the GTI by showing how uncompromising an electric GTI with motorsport ambitions can be. The concept car will be presented to the public next week at the Essen Motor Show (27 November to 6 December 2026). Its performance figures meet a two-door silhouette and flared wings as well as a large front splitter, diffuser and rear wing. The result: a powerful appearance and maximum downforce for fast laps. At the same time, the concept vehicle provides a preview of how the GTI idea can be further developed in the electric age.

In a recent development, kai Grünitz, Member of the Board of Management for Technical Development, Volkswagen Brand and Brand Group Core: “The GTI has been one of Volkswagen’s great success stories for 50 years. This year, we launched our GTI as an electric vehicle in series production for the first time. With the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, we are showing how much more potential there is in the electric GTI world. Our platform strategy and MEB+ give us the technological freedom to make even extreme concepts possible.”.

Recent findings suggest that designed for performance. The design of the latest ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is based on the production model, the 166 kW (226 PS) ID. Polo GTI. In both models, the drive power is transmitted to the front axle. In the 270 kW (367 PS) ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, this power delivery is controlled – thanks in part to an electronically regulated front differential lock (VAQ) – so that the model reaches 100 km/h from a standstill in just 4.7 seconds with Launch Control. Like the drive system, the electrical infrastructure has also been adapted to the high performance of the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept. The 52 kWh high-voltage battery can provide up to 290 kW at short notice, enabling a top speed of 240 km/h. The DCC (adaptive chassis control) has also been tuned for use on the racetrack and ensures precise handling and high traction in conjunction with the front differential lock. The new ceramic brakes of the one-box brake system are also designed for high performance.

Industry observers note that dynamics are visible in the design. On the exterior, the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept follows the powerful clarity of the ID. Polo GTI production model, while at the same time incorporating design elements that underline the motorsport characteristics. Particularly striking features are the two-door instead of four-door silhouette, pronounced flaring of the wings by 50 millimetres in each case, a large motorsport splitter at the front, a wider rear end, a upcoming diffuser and a rear wing in carbon fibre that protrudes above the roof line.

In a recent development, two-seater. Reduced to racing. The interior is also tailored to the racetrack, and only the basic layout of the overall cockpit has been adopted from the production model. This means there is no infotainment system, for example. The focus is solely on ergonomics and driving. The driver and front passenger sit on Recaro racing bucket seats with red 5-point harnesses. The rear and luggage compartment have been completely cleared. Instead of a rear seat system, a rollover bar painted in the GTI colour Tornado Red is integrated above and behind the front seats. The dash panel, side trims and many other details are covered in dark ArtVelours microfibre fabric with red topstitching – work that has been carried out with great precision by Volkswagen trainees. In many areas – in keeping with Volkswagen tradition – the young employees were directly involved in realisation of the concept vehicle by the Development department and designers.

Industry observers note that 550 instead of 290 newton-metres. The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept features the high-torque APP550 motor. The special technical challenge here: this motor is actually intended for the rear of large models such as the ID. Tiguan or ID.7. It therefore had to be fitted into the smaller ID. Polo as front-wheel drive and additionally combined with an electronic front differential lock. Thomas Schmall, Member of the Board of Management Volkswagen AG for Technology, and CEO of Volkswagen Group Components: “The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept shows just how emotive electric mobility can be: This is made possible by our APP550, one of the most efficient electric drives in its class. Manufactured over one million times at the Group Components plant in Kassel, this drive was actually developed for larger vehicle classes. Integrating it into the Polo required millimetre precision and is a powerful example of engineering skill and teamwork at Volkswagen, from Development and Design through to our trainees who worked on the project.”.

It has been revealed that GTI from the master of modular platforms. The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is based on the modular electric drive (MEB+) platform with front-wheel drive. Volkswagen has used the basic technical layout of the production model and taken it to a new level of performance with a 104 kW (141 PS) more powerful electric drive. The result is the most dynamic interpretation of a front-wheel drive ID. model to date. At the other end of the scale is the Mission Efficiency, which is also based on the ID. Polo and set four world records as a particularly efficient near-production electric vehicle. Both concept vehicles show the large bandwidth offered by electric drive systems from maximum sportiness to outstanding efficiency.

2026 is the year of the GTI. Following the Golf GTI EDITION 50, the upcoming ID.3 GTI (sales start early 2027) and the new ID. Polo GTI (available to order since October), the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is making its debut this year as the fourth new model under the umbrella of the iconic GTI product brand. No other compact sports car family has been as successful worldwide for half a century now – with more than 2.5 million units sold – as the GTI models.

energyRe Will Continue as Construction Manager Through Commercial Operation; Sale Reflects Strength of the Company’s South Carolina Development Platform; Transaction Expected to Close in First Quarter of 2027.

energyRe today announced that it has agreed to sell 100% of a portfolio of utility-scale solar projects in South Carolina to Enel Green Power North America, Inc. (EGPNA). The projects have a combined total capacity of roughly 317 MWdc of newly introduced generating capacity across the Palmetto State. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary conditions, including required U.S. regulatory approvals.

“This transaction is a strong validation of the projects we have built in South Carolina and of the team that developed them,” remarked Ryan Brown, Chief Operating Officer at energyRe. “Enel Green Power is a world-class owner and operator, and we are pleased to hand these projects to a partner that shares our commitment to delivering reliable, affordable power to South Carolina homes and businesses. Our team will remain on the ground as construction manager to see these projects through to commercial operation.”.

As part of the transaction, energyRe will continue to serve as construction manager through commercial operation.

energyRe has broken ground on approximately 450 MW in the last year and has nearly 700 MW in operation or late-stage development. The manufacturer’s 1.8+ GW portfolio spans 20 projects in South Carolina, North Carolina, Nebraska, and Oklahoma.

#122247. Industry News: The Legendary 1987 RUF CTR 'Yellowbird' Looks Like A Porsche, But It Isn't

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (814 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: The Legendary 1987 RUF CTR 'Yellowbird' Looks Like A Porsche, But It Isn't

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (814 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Take a quick look at that yellow beast in our top photo, with its bulging muscular fenders, curved profile, and massive whale tail spoiler.
  • In a recent development, there are a couple of dead giveaways, too, including the fact that the Yellowbird could outrun any real production Porsches of the time.
  • It has been revealed that of course, peeking under the skin of the Yellowbird tells the tale.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Take a quick look at that yellow beast in our top photo, with its bulging muscular fenders, curved profile, and massive whale tail spoiler. Now, you could easily be forgiven for thinking it was a Porsche — perhaps a late-1980s 911 Carrera 3.2. You'd be wrong, however. That machine is actually a Ruf CTR, which was nicknamed the Yellowbird for its striking exterior finish.

In a recent development, there are a couple of dead giveaways, too, including the fact that the Yellowbird could outrun any real production Porsches of the time. In fact, a Ruf CTR beat all challengers at a famed 1987 Road & Track comparison of the fastest cars in the world: Its 211-mph top speed was 10 mph faster than the second-place car, which was a modified Porsche, while entries like the AMG Hammer, Ferrari Testarossa, Lamborghini Countach, and Porsche 959 all failed to reach 200 mph. Unsurprisingly, the CTR was also named one of our readers' favorite yellow cars of all time.

It has been revealed that of course, peeking under the skin of the Yellowbird tells the tale. Keep in mind that Ruf is much more than just a tuning shop or an in-house performance brand, like Mercedes' AMG was and now is. Ruf uses so many proprietary components — and so few from production Porsche models — that it was certified as a full-on automaker back in 1981. Ruf cars even have different W09 VINs from Porsche's WP0 vehicle identification numbers. The genesis, though, actually does start with a Mercedes-Benz — well, that and a Porsche 356.

According to recent reports, the company now known as Ruf — pronounced roof – began when Alois Ruf Sr. opened his first repair shop in Pfaffenhausen, Germany, in 1939. Ruf and the shop would both survive World War II, and in the 1950s, he expanded into building his own tour bus — on a chassis originally sourced from Mercedes-Benz.

It was in 1963, when Ruf was at the wheel of his bus, that he happened to see a driver lose control of his Porsche 356 and run off the road. Ruf then played a key role in bringing both back to health: He drove the Porsche's owner to the hospital and — after buying it off of the insurer — took the car itself back to his shop to fix. That began a lifelong romance between the Rufs and rear-engined Porsches, and one that carried over to the launch of the 911. Today, 911s like the Carrera GTS T-Hybrid are still out there making the haters look real dumb.

We're going to skip a lot of steps in a pretty fascinating story, but Alois Jr. took over for his father in 1974 after the latter died. Under Alois Jr.'s direction, and in response to rumors Porsche would kill off the 911 after introducing the front-engine 928, the company committed itself to supporting the 911 even if Porsche didn't. The first Ruf-tuned 911, the Turbo 3.3, premiered in 1977 with a Ruf-built 5-speed manual transmission. However, legal worries soon reared their ugly heads. Porsche, naturally, wasn't too keen on being liable for what Ruf did to its cars, so Ruf would go on to officially become an independent automaker in 1981.

Yet, the car that really put Ruf on the map was the 1987 CTR, with a name derived from "Group C Turbo Ruf." The car started life as a 930-series 911 Carrera with a 3.2-liter flat-six engine, which was already one of the lightest models on the Porsche roster — it just wasn't light enough for Ruf. The firm swapped out the production doors, engine cover, and bumpers to save more poundage. The car even has just one sideview mirror. The rear fenders also were reworked, with flares to handle its upsized tire/wheel package and NACA ducts for engine cooling.

Ruf increased the bore of the Carrera's donor engine as well, boosting displacement to 3.4 liters. Remember, bore and stroke are the two specs that decide an engine's power. Next up were twin-turbochargers custom made for the Yellowbird and Bosch fuel injectors to slake the motor's thirst. The result was 469 horsepower and 408 pound-feet of torque. The 1987 Porsche 959, for some perspective, came out with a twin-turbo 2.8-liter flat-six factory rated for 444 horsepower and 369 pound-feet of torque.

The differences were even more noticeable on the track, as mentioned above. We'll also add that while the 959 was a tenth quicker to 60, at 3.6 seconds, the CTR could keep on going to reach 100 mph in 7.3 seconds. That's 1.5 seconds quicker than the 959. But if you really want to get a feel for what the Yellowbird was all about, be sure to check out Weissach Group's video of Ruf driver Stefan Roser running one at Nürburgring in 1989. It's downright fascinating.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Exhaust tips are the most visible parts of a car's exhaust system, making them a worthwhile option if you want to personalize your ride without spending a substantial chunk of cash on a complete aftermarket exhaust setup — especially if you don't want to risk voiding your warranty and ruining the mental peace of your neighbors. Available in different shapes, sizes, materials, and finishes, aftermarket exhaust tips can lend a sportier or more premium appearance to the car they're fitted to.

Industry observers note that that said, some believe that in addition to the aesthetic uplift, aftermarket tips can produce a deeper or louder exhaust note, help direct hot exhaust gases away from the rear bumper, and even improve your car's performance by reducing backpressure. What's fact, what's fiction, and do these benefits justify upgrading your car's factory exhaust tips?

The short answer is that aftermarket exhaust tips can offer some practical advantages, but they have next to no impact on performance and only a subtle effect on sound, at best. To understand what you gain from replacing them, it is crucial to distinguish between the exhaust tip and the components that actually determine how an exhaust system works.

According to recent reports, unlike the muffler, resonator, or catalytic converter, the exhaust tip doesn't really play a big role in controlling exhaust noise, emissions, or gas flow through your car's exhaust system. Its primary purpose is to finish the exhaust outlet, which is why aftermarket tips are available in several designs. These include straight-cut, angle-cut, rolled-edge, dual-exit, turndown, resonated, and dual-wall tips. Owners can also choose between finishes like polished stainless steel, chrome, matte black, and carbonfiber-like materials. Most aftermarket exhaust tips are pretty straightforward to install, with clamp-on and slip-on designs that directly attach to the existing tailpipe.

It has been revealed that there can be a minor change in exhaust sound, depending on the tip's diameter, length, shape, and the material used. A larger outlet may produce a somewhat deeper tone, while a longer tip can make your exhaust sound a little bit softer. A turndown tip directs exhaust gases and sound toward the ground, whereas a resonated tip can help reduce raspiness. To sum up, don't expect an aftermarket exhaust tip to make your daily-driver Toyota Camry sound like a V8-powered Lexus RC F.

One possible practical upside to an aftermarket exhaust tip is that it can help direct hot exhaust gases away from the bumper and surrounding body panels, and reduce soot accumulation around the outlet (particularly if you drive a diesel car), provided it is correctly sized and positioned. Stainless steel tips can additionally offer better rust resistance than some factory exhaust tips.

Despite what the marketing for some aftermarket exhaust tips may suggest, using them does not deliver a noticeable increase in power, torque, or overall performance. A common misconception is that a larger-diameter tip reduces exhaust backpressure, reducing the strain on the engine and thereby producing more power. However, since the tip is only the final outlet of the exhaust system, it has no effect on the system's overall flow characteristics. The diameter, length, and layout of the exhaust pipes, along with the design of the catalytic converter, muffler, and resonator, have a much greater impact.

Industry observers note that if you're looking for more noticeable changes in sound or performance, your best bet is to upgrade other components of the exhaust system. A performance muffler can deliver a more aggressive exhaust note and reduce backpressure, while an aftermarket resonator can give you finer control over sound. A cat-back exhaust system replaces the components from the catalytic converter to the tailpipe and can also offer a substantial change in sound and performance by dialing up the exhaust flow. Upgraded headers and high-flow catalytic converters are a couple more viable options to get a more aggressive exhaust note and boost performance.

Industry observers note that that mentioned, these modifications are considerably more expensive than an aftermarket exhaust tip, and may affect emissions compliance and noise levels, possibly even put you in trouble with the law. On the other hand, an exhaust tip is relatively cheap (prices start at around $20) and easy to install, and worth the effort if you want a better-looking rear end, a more durable exhaust outlet, or a minor change in sound. Just don't expect it to deliver the performance and aural benefits of a proper aftermarket exhaust system.

DTE Energy recently announced aims to add up to 150 megawatts of new solar energy in Michigan, a move that will create construction jobs, support local communities, and save customers money on fuel costs, the tech giant remarked.

According to recent reports, in addition, because solar generation does not require fuel, the latest projects will help reduce the tech giant’s exposure to changing fuel prices over their operating lives. The projects will also support DTE’s work to provide customers with energy that is reliable, increasingly clean, and affordable.

Sources indicate that the company stated that these projects are an investment in Michigan and its communities. By producing more Michigan-made energy that doesn’t require the purchase  of fuel, it can help lower energy costs for customers and reduce the reliance on fuel from outside the state. At the same time, these projects will create jobs and bring newly introduced investment and tax revenue into local communities, providing more resources for schools, first responders and the services Michigan families count on every day.

DTE is seeking competitive proposals for up to 150 megawatts of newly introduced Michigan-based solar generation. The procurement supports the requirements of the settlement agreement in Michigan Public Service Commission Case No. U-21662, approved May 15, 2025.

In a recent development, projects must achieve commercial operation by June 30, 2030, be located in Michigan and connect to either the MISO transmission system or DTE’s distribution system. Interested bidders can register and obtain additional information through PowerAdvocate. Proposals are due Jan. 19, 2027, and DTE expects to execute contracts in the second or third quarter of 2027.

DTE is a producer of and investor in renewable energy in Michigan, generating enough clean energy from wind and solar to power nearly one million homes. As the company works toward net zero carbon emissions, it remains committed to growing its renewable energy portfolio while maintaining a balanced mix of energy resources that supports reliability and affordability for customers. DTE’s 2026 Integrated Resource Plan builds on that commitment, calling for an additional 15 gigawatts of renewable energy by 2042.

In addition to the above issues, Waymo robotaxis have not operated appropriately at times when manual traffic control has replaced traffic lights. Waymo issued an revision recently following a crash that occurred as a result of this problem. “The ‌manual ⁠traffic recall is to ensure self-driving vehicles better responds to manual commands at intersections from law enforcement or other emergency personnel and follows a collision in which a Waymo followed directions from an officer, but the officer was then temporarily obstructed. That update was completed on November 6.”.

So, yes, Waymo robotaxis still aren’t perfect. However, Waymo continues to point out that its vehicles are much safer statistically than human-driven vehicles, as these vehicles are traveling far more miles between accidents than average human American drivers.

Jackery & Every Electric Transform Urban Energy Storage With Plug-In VPP

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1809 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, earlier this week, Jackery announced a strategic partnership with Brooklyn-based consumer energy aggregator Every Electric to offer the first plug-in Virtual Power Plant (VPP).
  • Recent findings suggest that the plug-in VPP costs customers nothing but earns them money by turning their household appliances into grid stabilizing assets.
  • As Every Electric puts it: “Get paid to plug in.” Alternatively, a customer can buy the batteries for a discounted price through the program of $650 and receive a higher payback per year, up to $250 per battery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, earlier this week, Jackery announced a strategic partnership with Brooklyn-based consumer energy aggregator Every Electric to offer the first plug-in Virtual Power Plant (VPP). The program starts with Upcoming York City apartment residents. I went to the RE+ in Las Vegas to meet with leaders from Jackery and Every Electric to learn more.

Recent findings suggest that the plug-in VPP costs customers nothing but earns them money by turning their household appliances into grid stabilizing assets. For the customer, the process is simple:.

That’s it. As Every Electric puts it: “Get paid to plug in.” Alternatively, a customer can buy the batteries for a discounted price through the program of $650 and receive a higher payback per year, up to $250 per battery. Over the 11-year rated lifespan, purchasing the battery could increase the total net payback, although the upfront cost would be a little higher.

In a recent development, it seems almost too simple and convenient for the customer. However, a lot of complex work and coordination is happening behind the scenes. The Jackery battery is in communication with Every Electric, who automates power management to charge when electricity demand is low and discharge to run the air conditioner when electricity demand is high. This kind of active demand response can go far beyond the typical TOU plan to directly mitigate utility demand shifts. Every Electric monitors data for each battery. The demand response of the combined storage across thousands of individual batteries is aggregated and sold to the utility, in this case Con Edison. Then the benefits are divided up and distributed to customers based on their contributions. Over 2000 batteries were in the initial trial phase, with a larger scale rollout planned next year. I am already on the waitlist, along with over 15,000 other NYC households.

Recent findings suggest that because it does not feed electricity back into the grid, implementation is much simpler. No electrician needed. The system monitors the amount of energy being stored and deployed at the point of use with no need for user intervention. Unlike traditional demand response that turns off appliances, there is no inconvenience to the user. Thermostats do not need to be adjusted. Smart appliances are not needed. The battery simply provides power when grid demand is high, shaving off the peaks.

Sources indicate that you may still be asking “what’s the catch?” Right now, the system needs to coordinate a large number of relatively small batteries under the same utility to have enough combined capacity to sell to the utility. To start, it is only being offered in New York City, which sets the blueprint. In the initial application, the batteries will be used with 120V air conditioners, up to around 12,000 BTU. This is a common size for NYC apartments, letting one battery size serve a wide range of customers, simplifying initial rollout. It also offers clear return on investment based on how much electricity is used, when that electricity is used and when demand peaks for the utility. However, I wouldn’t expect it to stop there.

The batteries being used are led by the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2. This battery has 2042 Wh of capacity and up to 2200 W of output with 4400 W of surge power. A total of three outlets are on the front panel, as well as two USB-C and a USB-A port. Due to the UPS function, the portable power station adds protection and would be ideal to plug in a computer or sensitive electronics, in addition to the air conditioner. Although the VPP is based on air conditioner use, using all the outlets can potentially add to the amount of load shifted by the VPP and, as a result, increase the amount of payback for the customer. Plugging in other forms of energy consumption could also extend the benefit beyond the times of year when the air conditioner is being used.

At 40% smaller and 34% lighter than the previous generation model, the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 weighs 39.5 lb. That’s less than a 5-gallon water cooler bottle but less bulky to carry. Due to the plug and play nature, people changing apartments within the city can easily take it with them at 13.2” x 10.4” x 11.5”. Multiple levels of safety protections and a ruggedized portable design using automotive-grade LFP batteries ensure safe operation even if apartment occupants bump into it.

That portability also contributes to the emergency preparedness capability of the battery. For the months of the year when the air conditioning isn’t running, the battery could provide backup power for a refrigerator in a power outage, for example. Of course, Jackery also offers batteries specifically for refrigerators. Those batteries are not a part of the initial program… yet.

In a recent development, this also gets to a limitation of the current program. To keep the program manageable as it scales up, only one size of battery in one use case is initially being offered. Right now, the biggest challenge is scaling up. Making it too complicated at the start would make scaling up more difficult. However, once the program reaches scale, more options can become available. Jackery also offers batteries with greater aesthetic appeal, like the slim FridgeGuard, which may be a better fit for the homes of some customers. As the program scales up, the applications have the potential to diversify.

Much of RE+ focused on supplying power and storage for data centers. While residential clean energy tax credits (25D) have been cut, data centers can still benefit from the Clean Electricity Investment Tax Credit that can add up with bonuses to cover half the cost of the project. With additional state and federal incentives piled on top, the majority of the cost of data center ESS can be covered by subsidies. With the heavily subsidized storage and large-scale contracts with the utility, data centers can access benefits not typically available to residential customers.

However, the plug-in VPP changes the energy storage dynamic. People get credit for energy storage deployment at the point of use. AI technology, rather than just being a consumer of resources, is being used to automate the VPP system and let the benefits flow to more families. By starting with small window air conditioners, the system also tends to provide relief to people living in typically older apartments, rather than the sleek fresh high rises with multi-million-dollar apartments.

There is no need for home electrical upgrades. In fact, by taking some of the load off the circuit, the potential for my wife to trip the breaker from ironing in the living room while the TV and air conditioner are running on the same breaker is reduced. As the energy monitoring comes directly from the battery, it also isn’t dependent on smart meters.

For the system to have enough total capacity to sell to the utility, the plug-in VPP needs to connect thousands of batteries to provide multiple MWh of storage. This scale can easily be accomplished in urban areas. In addition, the value of the system will heavily depend on the local price of electricity and the variability in price. In NYC, electricity is significantly more expensive than in most of the US.

Newly introduced York City apartments are a perfect starting place. While apartments tend to be far more energy efficient than detached houses and have lower net emissions overall, many of us living in apartments have traditionally felt a bit left out on clean tech. We don’t have roofs for rooftop panels. We typically do not have attached garages to place large permanent batteries or access to modify the electrical panel. If we do have the ability to make electrical modifications to the apartment, they can be prohibitively expensive in NYC. As such, a plug-in VPP is an exciting development for those of us living in apartments.

A plug-in VPP also makes the benefits of battery energy storage more accessible to urban areas. Often, there is not room for container-sized batteries. In places like New York City, the fire regulations are so strict, and the permitting is so complicated that large-scale BESS becomes exceedingly difficult to execute. Large-scale BESS, if approved, could take years to deploy.

According to NREL, the national average full installed price of utility scale BESS was $334/kWh of capacity in 2024, with hardware making up roughly two thirds of the total. However, the cost would undoubtedly be higher in NYC. For comparison, the discounted Explorer 2000 v2 in this program (which avoids retail markup) comes in at $318.32/kWh, with no added permitting or installation cost. That is also significantly less than the installed cost of many home batteries used in traditional VPPs, like Tesla Powerwall. Once delivered, it can be online within minutes.

Currently, plug-in VPP is the fastest, easiest and least expensive way to add battery capacity that shaves peak demand on urban grids in the US.

As high draw usage like air conditioning increases, more stress is placed on the grid. Transformer and other electricity transmission and distribution infrastructure upgrades can be expensive. Having storage at the point of use reduces the amount of electricity that needs to flow through the grid during peak periods. As plug-in VPP is deployed more broadly, the benefits will be experienced more broadly. And CO2 emissions can drop in the process.

While the benefits of the program are already attractive, the initial program may just be the tip of the iceberg. In New York City, buildings over 25,000 square feet must reduce their greenhouse gas emissions under Local Law 97 (LL97). This includes many apartment complexes and offices. The deployment of batteries at the point of use has the potential to reduce emissions.

While the current batteries and air conditioners in the program are 120V, Jackery also makes batteries that are 240V. For appliances that have intermittent use but high draw, like heat pumps, hot water heaters, ranges, etc., 240V connections are often needed to provide the necessary power. The electrification of applications that were previously run on gas or fuel oil can greatly reduce building emissions. But many apartment buildings do not have 240V outlets available. However, larger Jackery models can charge on 120V, accumulate charge and discharge at 240V for intermittent use. There is potential for batteries to support the higher voltage electrification without expensive electrical upgrades while also providing VPP benefit. The math would have to work out and it hasn’t happened yet. But the potential is clearly there.

Overall, the potential applications for this approach are massive. Already, I can see the potential to transform energy storage in NYC. In talking with Jackery and Every Electric, I started thinking about where the technology could go from here. Plug-in VPP could apply far beyond just Upcoming York City. However, that is for a follow-up article.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the average upcoming car price hits unrealistic highs, it only furthers the case for affordable vehicles. To provide some respite for desperate consumers, the Slate Truck no one can seem to stop talking about is coming soon in the U.S., and Italy's friendly but limited Fiat Topolino is breaching America's shores as well. The French, too, have come up with their own little practical, affordable utility EV, although this one is not coming to America. It's called La Bagnole. Points to the brand, Kilow, for the name, which translated to English is actually "the car.".

At first glance the little EV looks as if a Jeep and kei truck had a dependable, indestructible love child — indestructible simply because it's French. With the unrealistic expectations established in the "Carnage A Trois" episode of "The Grand Tour," where the trio tested the resilience of French cars in the "French way," by association these cars could be impossible to destroy, no?

According to recent reports, the beauty of it is, if La Bagnole is a little destructible and breaks, Kilow has designed repairs to be simple. And even the batteries can be fixed, as they house individually replaceable cells.

Sources indicate that the tiny tank of an EV truck is built on a steel chassis, with a customizable body. Customers can opt to have a removable roof color-matched to the body or go one further and also add transparent doors. Either choice allows the addition of optional roofbars for extra hauling ability. At the rear, flooring and tailgate can be Kilow's resinated wood fiber, which doesn't require any extra maintenance, while the Okoumé wood option does require the occasional varnishing. It also comes in at an extra 990 euros (about $1,100). If you prefer a more van-like delivery car look, there's a covered tailgate option as well.

Kilow markets La Bagnole as a simple vehicle. There are not a lot of parts to it, including no heating or cooling controls. What you can get is a minimalist dashboard made of the same resinated wood fiber or the Okoumé wood as well, fitted with a screen for battery updates, as well as toggle switches for the horn, wipers, washer fluid, and lights. You can really go all out and get a phone holder so you have your own navigation and tunes at the ready. No need to 3D-print it like you would have to for a Slate Truck.

Recent findings suggest that the vehicle's less simple side comes down to the color choices, of which there are 24. Twelve are solid colors, including quite the array across the rainbow, except for red and purple. Six gradient choices transition between two colors, and then there are the flecked colors reminiscent of a granite countertop, showing up as "Memories" on a page translated from French to English. Match those to steel or alloy rims, and mud guards for a polished look.

Power for La Bagnole is available in three battery capacities and ranges. Unlicensed drivers in France, likely more in city regions, can purchase two kinds of 28 mph batteries. The smaller of them is 6 kWh with a range of 43.5 miles, and the Long Range is a 12 kWh battery good for 102 miles. Licensed drivers can buy a 12 kWh battery with that same 102-mile range, but with a top speed of 50 mph. Charging can be done from a 220V household outlet, which Kilow says will take about three to five hours for a full charge, depending on the size of the battery.

Sources indicate that the accessories are fun as well. Avid campers can order a rooftop tent made by Decathlon, as long as you select a hardtop option. And if you about double the price of the tent, you can also get the camping kit complete with essential items like mugs, a coffee maker, stove and cooking pots, with the most attractive additions of the kit being the pressurized cooler, and pressurized shower. For the business-minded folks, you can also get your company logo added to the side panels, tailgate, and even the hardtop.

Industry observers note that each build takes about three months to complete, with prices ranging from 10,800 to 13,690 euros, which also includes the value-added tax (VAT). That's approximately $11,913 to $15,101 in the U.S. Yet as is the case for many fun vehicles made abroad, Americans will not be getting these little trucks as Kilow focuses sales on France and Europe. If we were to ever land these in the future, though, there could certainly be a case for using these utilitarian cuties across a good part of the country.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as the wind energy industry matures, operators and service providers are increasingly focused on maximizing turbine availability while controlling long-term maintenance costs. Although major drivetrain components often receive the spotlight, one overlooked system can have an outsized impact on turbine reliability and performance: gearbox oil cooling.

Industry observers note that heat exchangers play a critical role in maintaining proper oil temperature and viscosity within wind turbine gearboxes. When cooling systems become clogged with airborne debris, dust, or organic material, oil temperatures rise, lubrication performance declines, and component stress increases. Over time, these conditions can contribute to reduced gearbox efficiency, elevated maintenance demands, and avoidable downtime.

In a recent development, “Wind operators today are balancing increasing performance expectations with the realities of aging fleets and rising maintenance costs. Technologies that improve cooling efficiency and reduce service exposure can have a meaningful impact on long-term turbine reliability and operational profitability,” according to Mike Erickson, HYDAC’s Market Manager for the Wind Industry.

In a recent development, traditional “panel cut” heat exchanger designs have long been susceptible to clogging due to their tightly packed fin structures. In many wind environments — particularly agricultural, dusty, or high-pollen regions — debris accumulation can severely restrict airflow. Oil leaks can further compound the concern by trapping contaminants within the exchanger core, making cleaning more difficult and labor intensive.

This operational challenge has driven the need for more resilient cooling technologies designed specifically for real-world wind farm conditions.

HYDAC’s upcoming “Square Wave” heat exchanger design represents a significant advancement in addressing these reliability concerns. Engineered to allow debris to pass more freely through the exchanger fins, the design minimizes clogging while improving cooling efficiency under demanding operating conditions.

The importance of effective cooling cannot be overstated. Wind turbine gearbox oil typically operates within an optimal temperature range of approximately 45°C to 65°C. Even modest temperature increases can significantly impact oil viscosity. According to field data, a 12°C rise in oil temperature can reduce viscosity by nearly 28 percent — affecting lubrication quality and accelerating wear on critical drivetrain components.

It has been revealed that field trials have demonstrated measurable operational benefits from the Square Wave design. During a one-year trial on GE 1.x turbines, the upgraded exchanger consistently reduced clogging and lowered maintenance requirements compared to traditional panel cut cores. Operators reported reduced up-tower cleaning time and fewer temperature-related cooling faults.

Field validation across multiple turbine platforms has further reinforced the operational advantages of the Square Wave design. In one case study involving legacy 1 MW-class turbines operating in the Pacific Northwest, a major renewable energy operator installed pilot sets of Square Wave heat exchangers as part of a cooling performance evaluation. Installation teams reported the upgraded exchangers integrated seamlessly into the existing platform with no retrofit complications.

In a recent development, after initial operating data demonstrated improved cooling consistency, the operator expanded the evaluation program with additional units. Long-term SCADA analysis later indicated turbines equipped with Square Wave technology operate approximately 20 to 25 percent cooler than comparable turbines using conventional heat exchanger designs under similar operating conditions. The data also highlighted another crucial advantage: the Square Wave cores continued to maintain airflow and cooling efficiency in debris-heavy environments where traditional exchanger designs became increasingly restricted over time.

The successful deployment also generated interest from additional wind service organizations seeking retrofit-ready cooling upgrades that could improve turbine reliability while reducing maintenance burdens across aging fleets.

Industry observers note that “What operators are increasingly recognizing is that small improvements in thermal management can create meaningful gains in turbine reliability, maintenance efficiency, and long-term asset performance,” mentioned Erickson. “The field data we’re seeing continues to validate the value of designing cooling systems specifically for real-world wind operating environments.”.

More recently, long-term SCADA data from Mitsubishi platforms further validated the technology’s performance. After two years of operation, turbines equipped with Square Wave heat exchangers operated approximately 19 to 25 percent cooler than reference turbines using standard exchanger designs under comparable operating conditions.

For wind asset owners and service providers, the implications are substantial: Improved thermal management supports healthier oil viscosity, more stable gearbox operation, and potentially longer component life. At the same time, reduced cleaning frequency and fewer cooling-related service events translate directly into lower operational expenditures and increased turbine availability.

As the industry continues to prioritize lifecycle optimization and energy production efficiency, innovative subsystem upgrades such as advanced heat exchanger technology are becoming increasingly valuable. Rather than waiting for costly failures or performance degradation, operators are seeking practical retrofit solutions that improve reliability without requiring major system redesigns.

“Effective thermal management is critical to protecting gearbox health and maintaining oil performance over time. By addressing one of the most common causes of cooling degradation — debris accumulation — operators can improve uptime while reducing unnecessary maintenance interventions,” stated HYDAC’s Erickson.

It has been revealed that for wind stakeholders evaluating ways to improve gearbox reliability, reduce maintenance exposure, and enhance turbine performance, cooling system optimization deserves greater attention. Proven retrofit technologies like advanced heat exchanger designs can offer a practical path toward improved uptime and operational efficiency without requiring major system overhauls.

Industry observers note that as fleets age and performance expectations continue to rise, collaboration between operators, service providers, and technology partners will be essential to building more resilient wind assets for the future. Now is the time to evaluate whether existing cooling systems are supporting — or limiting — long-term turbine reliability goals.

Recent findings suggest that “HYDAC’s goal is to help wind owners and service providers solve practical operational challenges in ways that create long-term value across the entire asset lifecycle. Innovations like the Square Wave heat exchanger are designed to improve reliability, simplify maintenance, and support greater energy production over time.”.

Don’t let cooling system limitations impact turbine performance.

Proactive cooling optimization can help operators reduce maintenance exposure, protect critical drivetrain components, and maximize energy production across the asset lifecycle. Courts Are Undecided As To Whether Police Need Warrants For Flock Camera Data

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the operative word in this story's headline is "undecided." Because whether a police officer needs a warrant to use data obtained via Flock cameras seems to fall across multiple legalistic gray areas that aren't settled law.
  • Industry observers note that just for background (if you've been living in some paradise lacking this technology), Flock is a brand of device known as an automated license plate reader, or ALPR.
  • In a recent development, in the past we've reported on Flock cameras violating highway safety standards as well as the Fourth Amendment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the operative word in this story's headline is "undecided." Because whether a police officer needs a warrant to use data obtained via Flock cameras seems to fall across multiple legalistic gray areas that aren't settled law. Funny that our nation's founders didn't anticipate technology that surveils every driver (of course, they didn't anticipate cars, either).

Industry observers note that just for background (if you've been living in some paradise lacking this technology), Flock is a brand of device known as an automated license plate reader, or ALPR. And Flock contracts with law enforcement agencies across the country. Those agencies can opt to share their data with other police departments across a region, state, or the entire United States. In turn, that means police in many jurisdictions can use Flock to track anyone's movements nationally.

In a recent development, in the past we've reported on Flock cameras violating highway safety standards as well as the Fourth Amendment. But the meat of that latter nugget, of cops needing a warrant to obtain Flock camera data — or not needing a warrant — and whether that violates the Fourth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, is still up in the air.

According to recent reports, in case you're fuzzy on the law, the Fourth Amendment protects all of us against unreasonable searches and seizures. It requires law enforcement to have probable cause (i.e., reason to suspect a crime) in order to pull us over, search our cars, and fine or arrest us. The nub of this debate has  been addressed recently by judges in two states, and they've issued contradictory rulings about this very question: Do police need a warrant or don't they?

In a recent development, last month, at a federal district court in northern Oklahoma, Judge Sara Hill ruled that a Tulsa sheriff's deputy violated a defendant's Fourth Amendment rights when he used Flock's database to conduct a nationwide search on a Mazda SUV's previous location. The result: Pulling over 50 sightings from ALPRs across the U.S., he could see everywhere the car had been for the past 30 days.

In a recent development, but according to the ruling, the only reason for the officer's initial suspicion was that the Mazda SUV was from California. The officer followed the Mazda, noted a few driving infractions including following another car on the highway too closely, and pulled over the driver, Melissa Kyle. The traffic stop resulted in a search of Kyle's car, which led to Kyle's arrest on a charge of possession of marijuana. However, the charge was thrown out when Hill ruled that the officer's search of Flock data was unlawful and required a warrant. And so any evidence found subsequently was inadmissible.

According to recent reports, and yet a week later, an Ohio county judge ruled in an entirely opposite manner. Judge John Vavra of Belmont County Common Pleas Court ruled that a driver doesn't have a right to privacy that would restrict the use of Flock camera data.

Industry observers note that just to be clear, the federal court ruling is far more likely to lead to constitutional debate than a lower-level county case in Ohio. Court watchers say Hill's ruling is consistent with how the Supreme Court has declared certain mass-surveillance tech unconstitutional. And it's worth unpacking what happened in Oklahoma, because it illustrates how a police officer — with access to data via Flock — jumped to a conclusion that the judge in that case says violates the Fourth Amendment.

In 2022, we reported that Flock cameras could be used to track people traveling across state lines for abortion services. Then earlier this year 404 Media reported that cops in Texas did exactly that, tracking a woman via ALPR for seeking a legal abortion in another state.

The point of raising that matter is that the police didn't have a warrant for that ALPR search. The officer in Oklahoma also didn't have a warrant to search the movement of a car with California plates. The officer told Kyle that her long trip to and from California, spending only a little time there, had made him dubious about her — something he only knew about via Flock. Judge Hill found that the officer's logic didn't pass the test of reasonable suspicion and that, crucially, he decided to detain Kyle before he discovered that she had marijuana (recreational pot is illegal in Oklahoma).

Industry observers note that judge Hill ruled that the ALPR "... search was not supported by probable cause, and it was done without a warrant in violation of Kyle's Fourth Amendment rights." Hill found that ALPRs constitute "dragnet-style surveillance," and that "it becomes constitutionally problematic when law enforcement can indiscriminately and passively catalog your whereabouts ... and then use that information for any purpose whenever convenient.".

According to recent reports, we don't know whether Hill's ruling will carry up to higher courts. But this feels like the Fourth Amendment wreaking its own kind of vengeance. Especially because police have used Flock technology to stalk ex-partners, retaliate against police critics, racially profile minorities, and surveil protestors. Not to mention looking stuff up on Flock using search terms like LMAO. We're just journalists, not judges, but LMAO doesn't seem like probable cause. Nor does pulling the travel records of any car with out-of-state plates.

Solar module manufacturer Thornova Solar and Nextpower, a provider of advanced solar tracker and structural solutions, marked a milestone in their growing strategic cooperation with the signing of a Master Supply Agreement (MSA).

In a recent development, the agreement, announced at RE+ 2026, further strengthens the collaboration between the two companies, combining Thornova Solar’s U.S.-made solar modules with Nextpower’s U.S.-manufactured steel frame technology. The expanded effort is designed to deliver increased domestic content opportunities and enhanced structural performance, providing greater value to customers developing utility-scale and commercial and industrial (C&I) solar projects across the United States.

According to the companies, integrating advanced steel frame solutions into selected Thornova Solar module series addresses two increasingly crucial priorities in the U.S. solar market: maximizing domestic content and improving module resilience under demanding environmental conditions.

The combined solution offers several key benefits:.

The solution is particularly relevant for projects in demanding U.S. environments, including high-wind regions across the Midwest and Southeast, where structural reliability and long-term module performance are critical considerations.

Sources indicate that “The signing of this Master Supply Agreement represents an vital step in strengthening our relationship with Nextpower and expanding the value we deliver to U.S. customers,” remarked Andrea Bodenhagen, global marketing director of Thornova Solar. “By bringing together U.S.-made solar modules and domestically manufactured steel frame technology, we are helping our customers increase domestic content while benefiting from stronger, more resilient module solutions. This is exactly the kind of collaboration needed to advance a competitive U.S. solar manufacturing ecosystem.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re excited to deepen our strategic collaboration with Thornova and bring modules featuring Nextpower’s domestically manufactured steel frames to the U.S. market,” stated Jenya Meydbray, vice president and general manager of Nextpower. “NX CoreFrame offers a significant opportunity to advance module strength and reliability, addressing industry challenges such as glass breakage and demanding environmental loads while delivering greater confidence to solar developers and owners.”.

Sources indicate that the MSA reflects the shared commitment of both companies to strengthening domestic manufacturing and delivering solutions that respond to the evolving technical and commercial requirements of the U.S. solar market.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Navigating the world of Google Ads can be challenging, especially in an industry as competitive as real estate. One term you've probably heard in relation to Google Ads is "Quality Score." This score is crucial to how your ads perform and how much they cost. But what does it mean for realtors, and what constitutes a great Google Quality Real Estate Score? Let's dive in.

In a recent development, google Ads Quality Score is essentially a measurement of the quality and relevance of both your keywords and PPC ads. It is a dynamic metric, assigned on a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being the best possible score. It is used by Google to determine your cost per click (CPC) and your ad rank in the ad auction process.

Quality Score is calculated based on three primary components: click-through rate (CTR), ad relevance, and landing page experience.

For any industry, including real estate, a good Quality Score is generally around 7 or above. However, in the competitive world of real estate, striving for an even higher Quality Score could give you an advantage. So, for realtors, a great Quality Score might be considered 8 or above.

That mentioned, keep in mind that a high-Quality Score is not an end in itself. It's a sign that your ads are relevant, and your landing pages provide a good user experience, but it's still just one factor in the overall success of your Google Ads campaigns.

A high-Quality Score is beneficial for several reasons:.

Sources indicate that improving your Quality Score is all about relevance and user experience. Here are some strategies:.

A high Google Ads Quality Score can be a strong asset for realtors. It not only helps you rank higher and pay less for clicks but also ensures your ads are shown to the most relevant audiences. However, remember that Quality Score is just one piece of the puzzle. You should also consider other factors like your bidding strategy and overall account performance to create a successful Google Ads campaign.

With continuous effort and strategic planning, you can optimize your Quality Score and ultimately generate more leads for your real estate business.

#122221. EV Share Jumps to 68%(!) and Small BEVs Rise to Power — China EV Sales Report for October

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2019 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

EV Share Jumps to 68%(!) and Small BEVs Rise to Power — China EV Sales Report for October

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2019 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • High gas prices and a never-ending wave of fresh BEVs have allowed October to reach 68% EV market share, a new record!
  • According to recent reports, this record achievement is thanks to a significant ICE (internal combustion engine) crash.
  • According to recent reports, adding 45% BEV share to PHEVs (23% share) meant that in October a record 68% of all cars sold in China had a plug!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

High gas prices and a never-ending wave of fresh BEVs have allowed October to reach 68% EV market share, a new record!

According to recent reports, this record achievement is thanks to a significant ICE (internal combustion engine) crash. The overall market dropped 27% year over year (YoY), to around 1.6 million sales. Plugins were down 14% YoY, but pure ICE sales were much worse off, crashing 44% YoY!

According to recent reports, adding 45% BEV share to PHEVs (23% share) meant that in October a record 68% of all cars sold in China had a plug! If this trend continues in the future, the Chinese market will be fully electrified by 2030, and will be 100% BEV before 2035!

Industry observers note that this great result pulled the 2026 share up, to 59%, already 5% above the full year result of 2025. BEVs on their own were up to 40% (versus 33% in 2025).

At this pace, I expect the final number for 2026 EV share in China to be above 60%, with BEVs alone north of the 40% mark. And when the largest global automotive market gets this electrified … then the ICE industry is in serious trouble.

Sources indicate that the ICE extinction is also visible in the overall ranking. The overall top 10 was fully made by EVs. Again.

It has been revealed that looking at the best sellers in several size categories, the ICE extinction is also quite visible. Although, once again, the C-segment/compact category is the exception, with the only ICE representative showing up there — the Toyota RAV4, in 2nd, behind the leader Nevo Q05 and just ahead of the BYD Dolphin.

Having a quick look at the five size categories, the highlight is the B-segment/subcompact category, which is the hottest segment right now, with three of the top four top sellers in October belonging to this category.

Considering that 56% of the new SUVs introduced this year were bigger than 5 meters/197 inches, there is a clear disconnect between what people want (small hatchbacks/crossovers) and what OEMs offer (large SUVs).

Another highlight is the fact that Xiaomi had a gold plus silver win in the full size category, with the BYD Great Tang closing out the podium while the midsize category podium was 100% BYD Group.

Here’s more info and commentary on October’s top selling electric models:.

A BYD Dolphin for BYD Seagull money ($10,000). This was Geely’s internal memo to describe the formula for the Geely Xingyuan when developing its star model. With an interesting name — Xingyuan translates as “wishing upon a star” — it seems that Geely had its wish granted. However, the Geely model will have a tough adversary soon, as the latest generation Seagull will land with only one goal — to steal the Xingyuan’s best seller status. But while the new Seagull didn’t land, the small Geely scored a record performance in October, with its 50,190 registrations representing a 14% increase YoY. Besides the new BYD Seagull, Geely’s hatchback now has to deal with Leapmotor’s B-segment contenders, the A10 and A05; the new-generation Wuling Bingo; Chery’s new QQ3; and let’s not forget about BYD’s Yuan Up, too.

BYD’s midsize SUV continues to transition into the new generation. Thanks to the ramp-up of the new Ultra body, BYD’s star player was 2nd, scoring 30,772 registrations. Sales were up by 6% compared to the same month last year. The new Ultra generation features lidar and 1,500 kW DC charging, and these two features aren’t even the most impressive aspects of the model! That would be the price. It starts at 152,000 yuan (or $22,000) with the 76 kWh battery, and it goes up to 180,000 yuan (or $26,000) with the 83 kWh battery. For comparison, the Tesla Model Y starts in China at 259,000 yuan ($38,250)…. Expect the Song to experience a second youth from here onwards, and while it is impossible to displace the Tesla Model Y from the runner-up spot, the last place on the podium is doable this year. And maybe higher up in 2027?

Recent findings suggest that BYD’s small crossover continues to surprise, thanks to recently improved specs. BYD’s team player rose to 3rd in October, scoring 28,514 registrations, which was a 44% increase YoY and a upcoming record score. Despite not being the most exciting vehicle to look at, or drive, the truth is that it is surfing the wave of small, affordable EVs better than most, scoring high in value for money with prices starting at $11,000 and higher end versions having BYD’s driver-assistance system. With small vehicles at the moment having a moment in China, expect the small crossover to show up in the top 5 more regularly.

Sources indicate that things continue to go well for the startup brand, with its newly introduced baby A10 now established as the star player in an already strong lineup. Thanks to 27,247 registrations, the small crossover managed another top 5 presence. The model has the usual value-for-money focus of the brand, and a low, low price of 66,000 yuan ($10,000). On top of that, however, the A10 offers something close to a distinct personality, as the design eschews the white product standard design of Leapmotor for something more personal, mostly thanks to the front and back lights and a floating roof effect. With B-segment BEVs now being the hottest category in China, Leapmotor is well prepared to benefit from the subcompact rising tide, thanks to the recent arrival of the A10 small crossover and its sibling, the A05 small hatchback. Talk about perfect timing….

Sources indicate that after the SU7 and YU7, Xiaomi has another success on its hands. This big fat SUV — or shall I say SUVs, as the lineup is broken down between the 7-seat N90 and the 5-seat N70 — scored 27,132 registrations in only its second month on the market, pulling it immediately into the overall top 5. Even with the number of competitors growing every passing day, Xiaomi’s newly introduced land yachts have been selling like hot cakes, while drying up sales of the competition. Proof of that, is the fact that there were only two full size models in October’s top 20, with the other being … the Xiaomi SU7.

Looking at the rest of the best seller table, there were a number of models hitting record scores, starting with the #8 Nevo Q05 (20,022 units) continuing its success story. The #10 Bestune Xiaoma (17,887 units) benefitted from a recent refresh to score a surprise record score. Could this mean that small city EVs are (finally) seeing the light at the end of the tunnel?

As for the second half of the table, the highlight is the ramp-up of the Xpeng L03, with the attractive looking crossover, which kind of reminds of a mini-Lotus or small Polestar, reaching 13th thanks to 15,653 sales. This EV looks to be the startup’s star model thanks to a competitive price (124,000 RMB) that is half the price of the Tesla Model Y!

Other models with record performances were the #14 MG 4 (15,503 units), with the new generation proving to be much more popular and adaptable to local tastes than the previous one, and the #17 Chery QQ3 EV, which continued its slow climb in the ranking thanks to 14,041 sales, which made it the 5th B-segment model in the top 20.

In a recent development, still in the top 20, we should also highlight the best selling foreign model, the Tesla Model Y VW ID.Aura T6, the upcoming China-made (and China-developed) German crossover that has allowed Volkswagen to beat the Texans for the first time in years (the Tesla Model Y was down 60% YoY, to 7,807 units, while the Model 3 was down 85%, to 1,010 units). The Aura T6, VW’s take on the Model Y formula, rose to the 20th position in its first full month on the market!

Sources indicate that A promising sign, or just hype? Only time will tell, but at least for now, VW seems to be getting some traction on the EV side of the Chinese market, a point also highlighted by the fact that it wasn’t just the Aura T6 getting decent sales. The also fresh VW ID.Era 5S (think Chinese VW Jetta) got 7,100 registrations in October. Is there hope after all?

Industry observers note that outside the top 20, the main event was the ramp-up of Nevo’s latest baby, the Q06, which is looking to replicate the Q05’s success in the category above. With some 10,000 registrations in only its second month, it looks like it could join the top 20 soon. The same can be said about the Geely Galaxy TT, the make’s answer to the Xiaomi SU7, which had around 10,500 deliveries in October. Then there’s also the BYD Yuan Plus, which, after a long cross through the desert, seems to be picking up steam again. It scored 11,658 registrations last month, a new year best.

In a recent development, looking at the 2026 ranking, the podium remained the same, and unless something unexpected happens, it should stay as it is until the end of the year, with the small Geely repeating its 2025 win. That also means the Tesla Model Y will return to silver after getting bronze in 2025, and the BYD Song will get back onto the podium after a one-year absence.

Below the podium positions, though, there was some news. The BYD Yuan Up and Leapmotor A10 are surfing the B-segment wave and both climbed a position, to 5th and 6th, respectively.

If the BYD Yuan Up continues on its current record streak, then the small crossover could even aim to surpass the #4 FCB Ti7 before the year ends.

Still, with three subcompacts presently in the top 6 (Geely Xingyuan, BYD Yuan Up, and Leapmotor A10), small is hot right now, in China.

Elsewhere, the BYD Sealion 05 was up two positions, to 16th, while the Wuling Mini EV is hoping to bring tiny city cars back into the spotlight, and in October, it jumped two positions, ending the month in 13th….

Looking at the overall manufacturer ranking, it is a sea of red. Everyone is losing sales — big time. The exception is #5 Leapmotor (+31% YoY), while #8 Xiaomi (+3% YoY) and #10 Xpeng (+0%) are just hanging on.

So, now, not only are foreign OEMs suffering (Nissan was down 70% in October, Honda was down 51%), but even domestic ones are being affected by the EV shift.

Some may be asking, “But what about #9 Nevo and its 125% growth rate?” Well, it isn’t so much that they are winning sales, but they are effectively replacing the sales of their mother brand, Changan, which in October was only 19th after a 60% drop in sales YoY.

Looking at the auto brand ranking, BYD is firmly in the leadership position (17.2%), while runner-up Geely held to its 7.1% market share.

Rising 3rd placed Leapmotor (6.7%, up 0.2%) is fast approaching Geely. It wouldn’t be surprising if the startup brand became the new silver medalist in the final days of the year.

One thing is for certain though — Leapmotor will win its first medal this year. The only question is the material that it will be made of….

Speaking of position changes, Tesla had a horrible month (4.4%, down from 4.9% in September), which allowed Wuling (4.6%) to climb one position in October, into 4th. At the end of the year, expect Tesla to keep the #4 position, as its December peak should help it surpass Wuling.

Looking at OEMs/automotive groups/alliances, BYD is leading with 21.9% share of the market, up 0.1% in October.

Meanwhile, Geely remained in second with 11.8% share. The multinational conglomerate has the runner-up spot secured.

It has been revealed that #3 SAIC was stable (8%) and remained firm in the last place on the podium, while #4 Leapmotor (6.7%, up 0.2%) remained on the rise. Will we see the startup challenge SAIC in 2027 for the 3rd spot?

Ranking Today's 4 Main V12 Supercars By Horsepower As They Scream Into The Sunset

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1113 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, since burning tons of fuel to move one, maybe two, people around isn't the greatest thing for the planet, massive V12 engines are a dying breed.
  • And for the supercar geeks about to run to the comments to point out that one McLaren F1-shaped omission, Gordon Murray's T.50 did indeed use a V12 — a naturally aspirated 3.9-liter developed by Cosworth, no less — but that car actually ended production back in the summer of 2025, so it's out of the running.
  • Despite ranking at the bottom in terms of power, the Ferrari 12Cilindri is arguably, for one obvious reason, the car most overtly proud of the fact that it still uses a V12 — that name, by the way, is pronounced "dodici cilindri," where the first c is a "ch" sound.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, since burning tons of fuel to move one, maybe two, people around isn't the greatest thing for the planet, massive V12 engines are a dying breed. Even among supercars, there are pretty much only four left that use what is arguably the most romantic engine layout possible. You can count 'em on one hand: there's a Ferrari, a Lamborghini, an Aston Martin, and a Pagani. If you're curious as to how they rank purely in terms of horsepower, you've come to the right place.

And for the supercar geeks about to run to the comments to point out that one McLaren F1-shaped omission, Gordon Murray's T.50 did indeed use a V12 — a naturally aspirated 3.9-liter developed by Cosworth, no less — but that car actually ended production back in the summer of 2025, so it's out of the running. In a similar vein, the Aston Martin Valkyrie indeed made enough power to sit atop this list, but production stopped back in 2024. Without further ado, then, here are today's four main V12 supercars, ranked by horsepower.

Despite ranking at the bottom in terms of power, the Ferrari 12Cilindri is arguably, for one obvious reason, the car most overtly proud of the fact that it still uses a V12 — that name, by the way, is pronounced "dodici cilindri," where the first c is a "ch" sound. The cilindris in question are inside a 6.5-liter naturally aspirated V12 making 819 hp. The 12Cilindri can go from zero to 62 mph in 2.9 seconds and has a top speed exceeding 211 mph. While mighty by any standard, forward thrust plays second fiddle to this engine's real allure: a sky-high redline of 9,500 rpm.

In a recent development, in regular form, those revs generate power going to the rear axle through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. The recent big news about this car, however, is the introduction of a Manuale variant that pairs that V12 with a gated "manual" transmission that is, in reality, a meticulously programmed simulation of a three-pedal gearbox. There's been much debate over whether the Manuale's authenticity matters, but I'm just glad its screaming V12 remains a genuine article.

Besting its Ferrari rival by precisely 5 hp is the Aston Martin Vanquish. Where the 12Cilindri is staunchly naturally aspirated, the Aston makes its power with forced induction, adding two turbos to its 5.2-liter V12 to make 824 horses. Zero to 60 mph is achieved in 3.2 seconds, and it'll hit a top speed of 214 mph.

Industry observers note that it's a real Aston engine, too, because unlike the Mercedes V8s you find in the brand's modern Vantage and DBX, this V12 is a continuation of the in-house motor that powered the old DB11 and DBS Superleggera. In addition to stronger connecting rods, higher flow-rate fuel injectors, and quicker turbos, this motor gets a fresh Boost Reserve function that builds boost in the background during partial throttle so it's ready to go when you do floor it. I've driven it, and in practice, the Vanquish pulls off the Aston Martin thing of being just as exciting as a sporting machine as it is livable and comfortable as a GT car.

Recent findings suggest that like any good exotic automaker, Aston loves a good limited-run special model, and, for posterity, the Vanquish-based Valen takes this engine and makes a slightly nuttier 838 hp. There's also a 705-hp, manual-transmission Valour, plus a more track-focused, 735-hp variant called the Valiant. As if being a manual V12 Aston made for the track wasn't cool enough, that last one happened to come about as a personal commission from two-time world champ and Aston Martin Formula 1 driver, Fernando Alonso.

According to recent reports, when it comes to pure horsepower, none of Aston's current V12 fare beats the Pagani Utopia. An exotic among exotics, the Utopia is powered by a twin-turbocharged 6.0-liter V12, made just for this car by Mercedes-AMG, pumping out a mighty 864 hp.

Industry observers note that you can get the Utopia with a seven-speed automated manual gearbox, but I'm not sure why you would when the seven-speed actual manual is right there. In true Pagani fashion, it has a gated gearbox where the entire shift linkage is exposed and shiny and glorious. Zero to 60 mph is said to take around 3.0 seconds, and the Roadster is electronically limited to 217 mph, but tellingly, a lot of Pagani's own literature shies away from discussing such specs.

In a recent development, this is not a car that seems to concern itself much with instrumented testing — you wouldn't strap a stopwatch to the Mona Lisa, now would you? To put it another way: the Pagani Utopia is arguably the car on this list I'd be in the most awe of coming across in the wild, and that insane 864-hp V12 somehow isn't even in the top three reasons that's the case.

Recent findings suggest that if technical dominance is what you're after, the most powerful V12 supercar on the market today is the Lamborghini Revuelto SV, which makes 1,050 horsepower. Mind you, that doesn't come solely from its naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12. Instead, it's a culmination of that engine plus three hybrid electric motors — yep, in case you missed the memo, both of Lamborghini's supercars are now plug-in hybrids.

It has been revealed that in a parallel universe where the Revuelto wasn't a hybrid, however, it'd come last on this list because its V12 alone produces "just" 814 hp, six fewer ponies than that equally large Ferrari motor. But that's not how the game is played.

Taken as a whole, the electrified Lambo gets from zero to 62 mph in just 2.4 seconds, notably quicker than every other car here, and it reaches a top speed of 216 mph. The fastest and most powerful production Lamborghini ever dominates on a dragstrip not just on the back of its immense horsepower but also because it's the only car on this list with all-wheel-drive. Each front wheel is powered by a dedicated electric motor (the remaining e-motor is at the back, helping out that V12).

As it happens, I was fortunate enough to drive a "regular," non-SV Revuelto last year, which made a relatively paltry 1,001 hp. The speed was, in a word, ridiculous, and that V12 soundtrack remains an absolute treat. In the admittedly small pantheon of V12 supercars that remain, the Ferrari may be more pure, the Aston more refined, and the Pagani more special, but in the contest of pure horsepower and speed, the Lamborghini Revuelto, for now at least, sits at the peak.

Maybe Don't Paint Your Car With House Paint

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (328 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the mates at Australia's creative Garbage Time have done it again.
  • According to recent reports, you may be surprised to hear this, but no — covering a house-painted car in dust, dirt, pollen, and bird droppings does not, in fact, improve the quality of the paint.
  • After a year of dealing with outdoor conditions, the Corolla's paint is pretty thoroughly wrecked, which is saying something for a carmaker noted for its terrible colors.

According to recent reports, the mates at Australia's creative Garbage Time have done it again. Last year they painted a Toyota Corolla entirely with house paint, more or less color matched to the car's existing paint by a local hardware store chain. This turned out to be a bad idea, as house paint is fundamentally very different from your favorite automotive paints, but then the geniuses behind the channel had a brain blast: Leave the car outside, parked under a tree, for a year. Surely that would make things better, right?

According to recent reports, you may be surprised to hear this, but no — covering a house-painted car in dust, dirt, pollen, and bird droppings does not, in fact, improve the quality of the paint. Washing it afterward doesn't help, either, because a touchless wash can't really get anything out of that soft, ductile paint. No, once you've covered your car in hardware-store house paint — without any preparation, primer, or clear coat — you're pretty much screwed.

After a year of dealing with outdoor conditions, the Corolla's paint is pretty thoroughly wrecked, which is saying something for a carmaker noted for its terrible colors. A touchless wash did absolutely nothing to fix that, and even a hand wash was only a marginal improvement. The house paint, constantly referred to as "gummy" throughout the video, is just too good at grabbing onto dirt and holding onto it. It's also pretty great at peeling off the car when aggressively cleaned.

From a distance, the house-painted Corolla actually doesn't look terrible — a bit wet, like the paint isn't fully dry, but not uncannily so. It's clearly not a factory paint job, but from 20 feet away you'd be hard-pressed to tell this automotive travesty from a poor rattlecan job that combined proper materials with improper technique. This Corolla got neither the right stuff nor the right methods. But hey, at least it was cheap.

In a recent development, the digital world has revolutionized how real estate is marketed and sold, placing a premium on strategic online presence and data-driven advertising.
